articles.title: Una nube europea con cifrado postcuántico para evitar problemas de seguridad futuros: Internxt sigue con su promo estrella activa
articles.text:
Aunque suene un poco a ciencia ficción, la computación cuántica está cerca de ser una realidad a gran escala. Pero, ¿y eso en qué nos afecta a nosotros? Este tipo de ordenadores, entre otras muchas cosas, son capaces de descifrar los sistemas de cifrado que más se utilizan hoy en día. Por eso mismo, ya hay varias compañías preparándose para hacerle frente a este nuevo escenario y una de ellas es Internxt, servicio de almacenamiento en la nube que cuenta con cifrado postcuántico.
Internxt Drive
Un servicio de almacenamiento preparado para el futuro
La computación cuántica es un desafío para la ciberseguridad actual y del futuro. Todos los servicios en la nube utilizan algoritmos y sistemas de cifrado para proteger sus datos que no son capaces de resolver los ordenadores actuales dada su complejidad. Ahí es donde entran los ordenadores cuánticos, que trabajan de una forma radicalmente diferente y sí que son capaces de romper estos sistemas actuales. Dicho de otra forma: los sistemas de seguridad que se usan ahora mismo podrían dejar de ser seguros en un futuro.
En este punto, es posible que pensemos que, como los ordenadores cuánticos no son una realidad todavía, no tenemos que preocuparnos por ellos. Esto no es así del todo, ya que alguien puede interceptar nuestros datos y almacenarlos de cara al futuro. Puede que estos no sean accesibles en la actualidad por los sistemas de cifrado que se están usando ahora mismo, pero sí que lo serían con la computación cuántica.
No es ninguna locura que nuestros datos, incluso protegidos por algoritmos seguros, se queden almacenados durante muchos años. Hay ciertos tipos de información que quizás no sean un problema, pero otros, como documentos de identidad o fotografías, sí. En ese sentido, merece la pena proteger nuestros datos de las amenazas actuales, pero también de las futuras.
Precisamente por eso, Internxt tiene su almacenamiento en la nube preparado para evitar estos riesgos. Esta compañía ha incorporado a su servicio los algoritmos Kyber-512 y AES-256, diseñados específicamente para hacer frente a las futuras capacidades de los ordenadores cuánticos. De esta forma, incluso si nuestros datos acaban almacenados en algún lugar, tampoco podrán ser descifrados.
A esto, hay que sumarle que Internxt utiliza una arquitectura de conocimiento cero. Eso quiere decir que nuestros datos se cifran antes de subirse a la nube y no al llegar a esta, por lo que, incluso si alguien los intercepta en el camino, ya estarán cifrados. Además, como es de código abierto, cualquier persona puede auditar el servicio para comprobar que no existe ningún tipo de puerta trasera para acceder a nuestros datos.
Internxt Drive
Si estás buscando un nuevo servicio en la nube, Internxt te puede encajar muy bien, especialmente si tenemos en cuenta que, utilizando el código 'XATAKA', sus planes tienen un 90 % de descuento. El plan más económico cuesta 190 euros y tendremos servicio para toda la vida. Y no solo almacenamiento en la nube: también antivirus y VPN.

articles.title: Reinventing hiring for the AI-driven labor market
articles.text:
Reinventing hiring for the AI-driven labor market
From talent scouts to talent architects
Recruitment has always reflected the realities of the labor market it serves. For decades, those realities were relatively stable.
Roles were well defined, career paths followed familiar patterns, and organizations could afford to move at a measured pace when bringing in new talent. That context has changed, but many hiring practices have not.
Today, skills evolve quickly, business priorities shift frequently, and candidates expect a level of speed and transparency that traditional processes struggle to provide.
The result is a growing mismatch between what organizations need and how they go about finding it.
Chief People Officer, Version 1.
Hiring cycles stretch out, decisions are made with incomplete information, and opportunities to secure the right talent are often missed.
It is within this context that artificial intelligence has entered the conversation, often accompanied by a degree of unease. Questions about automation, control, and fairness are not only understandable but necessary. However, focusing too narrowly on whether AI might replace elements of HR risks overlooking the more important development taking place.
There has been a rapid rise in the technology, with 87% of companies now adopting AI to support recruitment . AI is reshaping how decisions are made, and in doing so, it is redefining the contribution HR can make to an organization.
Sign up to the TechRadar Pro newsletter to get all the top news, opinion, features and guidance your business needs to succeed!
Establishing talent architects
For many HR teams, a significant proportion of time is still absorbed by coordination and administration. Screening applications, arranging interviews, and managing workflows are essential tasks, but they rarely represent the highest-value use of expertise.
A recent study three quarters of recruiters are using AI to save time and improve sourcing candidates . AI has the potential to absorb much of this operational load, processing large volumes of information quickly and consistently, while identifying patterns that would be difficult to detect through manual methods alone.
The benefit generates efficiency, while also creating the opportunity for HR leaders to operate with greater strategic intent. As organizations adopt AI-enabled approaches, the role of HR begins to move away from managing transactions and towards shaping the workforce more deliberately.
The concept of the HR leader as a “talent architect” is increasingly relevant in this environment. It reflects a responsibility not just to fill roles, but to design teams around capability, potential, and long-term direction. This requires a different balance of skills, combining an understanding of data and technology with a strong grounding in judgement, experience, and organizational culture.
Improving fairness through greater visibility
Concerns around bias often sit at the center of discussions about AI in hiring. There is a legitimate fear that automated systems could reinforce existing inequalities if left unchecked. Yet it is also important to recognize that bias is not introduced by technology alone. It is already present in many traditional hiring processes, often in ways that are subtle and difficult to measure.
What AI offers, when implemented with care, is greater visibility. Patterns in decision-making can be analyzed, inconsistencies can be identified, and outcomes can be assessed against clear criteria. This does not remove the responsibility from organizations to act, but it does provide a stronger foundation for doing so. Effective governance, transparency in how systems are trained, and ongoing review are essential if these benefits are to be realized.
Alongside considerations of fairness, there is a broader question of how AI influences the human aspects of hiring. The risk is not that technology replaces judgement, but that it is relied upon too heavily without sufficient oversight. The most effective organizations will be those that treat AI as a source of insight rather than a substitute for decision-making.
When this balance is achieved, the impact is tangible. Hiring processes become more responsive, with fewer delays between stages. Decisions are supported by a richer evidence base, allowing for greater confidence in outcomes . Candidates experience a process that is more consistent and easier to understand, which in turn strengthens the organization's reputation as an employer.
A better outcome for businesses and candidates
There are also clear links to business performance. When hiring decisions are better aligned with the capabilities required, organizations are more likely to see improvements in productivity and retention. Teams are built with an eye on future needs as well as immediate demands, which is particularly important in sectors where change is constant.
At the same time, candidates benefit from a process that is more transparent and consistent. Decisions are grounded in evidence, and opportunities are matched more closely to individual strengths. The experience becomes more predictable and, ultimately, more credible.
For HR leaders, the priority now is to approach AI with both ambition and discipline. Introducing new tools without a clear understanding of the problem they are intended to solve will deliver limited value. Equally, adopting a cautious stance that delays progress may leave organizations at a disadvantage in a competitive talent market.
Clarity of purpose is therefore essential. Whether the objective is to reduce time-to-hire, improve the quality of matches, or strengthen diversity, the role of AI should be defined in relation to those outcomes. This should be supported by investment in capability, ensuring that HR teams are equipped to interpret and apply the insights generated.
Perhaps most importantly, there needs to be a shift in how the role of HR is perceived within the organization. The introduction of AI does not diminish the importance of human expertise; it places a greater emphasis on it. As routine tasks are streamlined, the expectation is that HR will contribute more directly to strategic decision-making, bringing a deeper understanding of talent, culture, and organizational dynamics.
A new chapter for hiring
Companies integrating technology into their recruitment operations have seen their hiring processes become faster, data-informed, and more closely aligned to business priorities. AI is a significant factor in that transition, but it is not the defining feature. Rather, HR existing with AI support depends on how organisations choose to integrate technology with human judgement.
For those that do this well, the outcome is greater than a more efficient hiring process. It is a more thoughtful and effective approach to building teams, one that recognises both the value of data and the importance of human insight.
That balance will shape the next phase of hiring, and it will determine the extent to which organizations are able to adapt to the demands of an increasingly dynamic labor market.

articles.title: Databricks and Microsoft expand Azure partnership into the 2030s - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
Databricks and Microsoft expand Azure partnership into the 2030s
Databricks Inc. and Microsoft Corp. today said they’re extending their strategic partnership into the 2030s as the companies seek business from enterprises building artificial intelligence applications grounded in proprietary data and business context.
Under the expanded agreement, Databricks will increase its use of Microsoft Azure to operate its own business. The company plans to run core operations and analytics on Azure Databricks while building its unified data lakehouse on the platform.
Databricks will also expand its use of Azure Cobalt, Microsoft’s Arm-based computing infrastructure, for data-intensive and agentic AI workloads. Databricks currently uses Cobalt 100 processors and plans to adopt Cobalt 200, which Microsoft says delivers up to 50% better performance and provides memory encryption by default.
Microsoft, in turn, said it will continue integrating Databricks’ data and AI technology across products that include Microsoft 365, Teams, Copilot, Power BI, OneLake, Purview and Microsoft Foundry.
The integrations will include Databricks Genie, an AI assistant that connects users and agents with an organization’s business data. Genie Ontology provides the business concepts and relationships needed to interpret that data, while Unity AI Gateway gives companies a centralized way to govern models, agents, usage and costs.
The companies are targeting a persistent obstacle to enterprise AI adoption: Although organizations possess large amounts of operational data, they often struggle to connect models and agents to trusted business knowledge while maintaining security, governance and cost controls.
“The next generation of AI will be defined by how effectively organizations turn their unique knowledge into intelligence,” said Judson Althoff, chief executive of Microsoft’s commercial business. He said Databricks’ increased use of Azure Databricks and Cobalt infrastructure should improve performance, efficiency and scalability.
The companies said Azure Databricks is already used by thousands of organizations, including Banco Bradesco SA, Electrolux AB, Sumitomo Mitsui Banking Corp., Unilever PLC and Major League Baseball’s Cincinnati Reds.

articles.title: Free corrige un bug Wi-Fi qui embêtait les abonnés Freebox, qui doivent mettre leur appareil à jour
articles.text:
Free a déployé la mise à jour 4.12.3 pour ses Freebox Server jeudi matin. Elle corrige un bug Wi-Fi 5 GHz capricieux ainsi que les icônes disparues du journal d'appels FreeboxOS, attendues par les abonnés.
Entre un Wi-Fi 5 GHz parfois capricieux et un journal d'appels devenu difficile à lire, les utilisateurs de Freebox Server (Revolution, Pop, Delta et Ultra) avaient de quoi pester ces derniers temps. Le second souci a d'ailleurs connu un traitement express en interne chez Free, confirmé en seulement deux jours par les équipes techniques, avant d'être officiellement intégré à la version 4.12.3. On fait le point sur ce que change concrètement cette mise à jour déployée ce jeudi 23 juillet, et surtout, sur la marche à suivre pour l'installer sans prise de tête.
Un bug Wi-Fi et des icônes qui reviennent enfin : la Freebox se met à jour
Dans de rares cas, les cartes Wi-Fi 5 GHz pouvaient rester coincées en mode DFS, un protocole de sécurité qui oblige la box à surveiller la présence de radars sur la fréquence utilisée, pendant une durée bien plus longue que ce qui était initialement prévu. Un bug discret, difficile à repérer pour la plupart des abonnés, mais que Free a jugé suffisamment gênant pour le corriger dans cette livraison.
L'autre correctif, plus visible cette fois, concerne le retour des icônes dans le journal d'appels de FreeboxOS. Disparues depuis plusieurs semaines, elles permettaient pourtant de distinguer d'un coup d'œil un appel entrant, sortant ou manqué, un détail d'ergonomie peut-être mais qui, une fois absent, se remarque vite. Le bug avait été signalé très récemment, à la mi-juillet, et avait recueilli le soutien d'autres abonnés visiblement gênés par le même souci.
L'auteur du signalement avait lui-même mis le doigt sur l'origine du problème, une simple propriété de hauteur manquante dans une feuille de style de l'interface, et proposé la correction exacte à appliquer. Un travail de débogage presque bénévole, salué deux jours plus tard par un administrateur Free, qui a confirmé que le correctif serait bien intégré au prochain firmware, celui-là même qui vient d'atterrir sur nos Freebox Server.
La marche à suivre pour profiter de la version 4.12.3
Comme d'habitude, aucune manipulation complexe n'est nécessaire de votre côté. La version 4.12.3 est mise à disposition directement par Free, sans installation manuelle à effectuer. Il suffit de redémarrer votre Freebox Server, soit directement depuis le boîtier, soit via l'application Free ou l'interface FreeboxOS, pour que les correctifs soient effectivement appliqués.
Pour vérifier que la mise à jour a bien été installée, vous pouvez passer par l'application Free ou, à l'aide des flèches de votre Server, suivre le menu « Système » puis « Version » (pour les Revolution, Mini 4K, One), simplement « Version » (pour la Delta), ou « Informations avancées » puis « Version » (pour les PopetUltra). De quoi confirmer en quelques secondes que votre Freebox tourne bien sous la dernière mouture du logiciel.

articles.title: Apple se lanza a grabar novelas usando solo el iPhone 17 Pro: Nido de Villanas ya disponible
articles.text:
Apple presentó Nido de Villanas, una micronovela en formato vertical grabada íntegramente con iPhone 17 Pro. La serie, compuesta por catorce episodios breves, marca la incursión de la compañía en un género emblemático para México y América Latina.
Desde el 21 de julio, los episodios están disponibles en el canal de YouTube de Apple y en la plataforma streaming ViX. La producción reúne a figuras reconocidas de la telenovela, como Itatí Cantoral, Gabriela Spanic, Ela Velden, Mariana Torres, Carlos Said, Luis Fernando Peña y Omar Fierro.
PUBLICIDAD
El guion fue escrito por Gustavo Bracco, conocido por su trabajo en títulos como “Vencer el miedo” y “Vencer el desamor”, mientras que la dirección estuvo a cargo de Salvador Espinosa, responsable de episodios en series como “Club de Cuervos” y “El teniente Harina vs. el Cancelador”.
Cómo influyó el uso del iPhone 17 Pro en la producción de la micronovela
La totalidad de la grabación se realizó utilizando un iPhone 17 Pro, dispositivo que incorpora herramientas de video avanzadas, entre ellas el formato Log, que permite una corrección de color profesional, y el modo Cine, que facilita el enfoque selectivo y la profundidad de campo característica del cine tradicional.
PUBLICIDAD
Además, la compatibilidad con Dolby Vision y la resolución 4K formaron parte del proceso técnico. Durante el rodaje, el director de fotografía Alexis Zabé aprovechó estas capacidades para dotar a la serie de una estética cuidada y adaptable a los estándares de calidad de la televisión y el streaming.
Zabé ya había colaborado previamente con Apple en el cortometraje “El lazo de Petra”, donde exploró de igual forma las posibilidades del video desde el celular.
PUBLICIDAD
Qué diferencia a Nido de Villanas dentro del género de la telenovela
Nido de Villanas recupera elementos clásicos de la telenovela mexicana, como la ambición, los secretos familiares y las traiciones, y los traslada a relatos breves optimizados para el consumo digital.
La historia gira alrededor de cuatro mujeres que compiten por la fortuna de la familia Iturribiaga, núcleo de conflictos y alianzas temporales, según la sinopsis oficial publicada en YouTube.
PUBLICIDAD
La serie apuesta por el microdrama, un formato que ha ganado popularidad especialmente entre la generación Z. Cada episodio tiene una duración reducida, lo que facilita su visualización en dispositivos y plataformas sociales.
Dónde y cuándo se puede visualizar Nido de Villanas
Los catorce episodios de Nido de Villanas se encuentran disponibles desde el 21 de julio tanto en el canal de YouTube de Apple como en la plataforma ViX. El acceso es gratuito, lo que amplía el alcance potencial de la serie entre usuarios de diferentes regiones.
PUBLICIDAD
La selección de estas plataformas responde a los hábitos de consumo de la audiencia más joven, que prioriza el acceso instantáneo y multiplataforma. El formato vertical de la serie facilita la visualización en smartphones y tablets.
Qué otras producciones cinematográficas se han grabado con un iPhone
Apple ha impulsado el uso de sus dispositivos en producciones audiovisuales internacionales. La película F1 (2025), dirigida por Joseph Kosinski y protagonizada por Brad Pitt y Damson Idris, incluyó secuencias grabadas con iPhone 15 Pro Max y tecnologías propias como ProRes y Apple Log.
PUBLICIDAD
El objetivo fue capturar escenas de pista y planos subjetivos con un realismo difícil de lograr con cámaras tradicionales.
En el ámbito del cine de terror, 28 años después (2025), dirigida por Danny Boyle, también utilizó el iPhone 15 Pro Max para secuencias en condiciones de poca luz, logrando una estética cercana al documental.
PUBLICIDAD
Asimismo, la pionera en este campo fue Tangerine (2015), filmada completamente con un iPhone 5s, que marcó un precedente en la adopción de la tecnología móvil por parte de cineastas independientes.

he Philips dual-sided business monitor 24B2D5300 has just been announced and it is the first standalone monitor to incorporate a unique "dual screen" design. With a screen on each side of the device, the monitor opens up new opportunities for business workflows, customer-facing applications, and collaborative use.
This monitor is equipped with two 23.8" IPS technology panels, Full HD resolution on both screens, 120 Hz refresh rates, and USB-C connectivity for seamless connection into existing modern hardware. While the monitor offers a strong feature set, its true differentiation lies in a unique dual-sided design and bespoke build to ensure users get the most out of the dual screens.Powering modern customer-facing environments with SmartView and DualView
The Philips dual-sided business monitor unlocks new opportunities for businesses with a "front-desk" experience. SmartView and DualView introduce an innovative way to manage what is shown on each side of the display. While SmartView allows content to be split into two virtual sections from a single device input, DualView enables the rear screen to mirror or extend the primary display. This enables experiences tailored to customers or visitors.
On the business side, users can keep applications and sensitive information visible only on one side of the monitor, while the customer-facing screen presents relevant content such as purchase details, interactive applications, or personalised information. This clear separation enables businesses to provide engaging customer experiences without compromising efficiency or privacy.
The dual-sided 24B2D5300 is well-suited for a wide range of professional environments, including offices with reception areas, banks, healthcare facilities, service counters, and many other customer interaction scenarios. It can support a seamless check-in process, real-time customer interactions, and secure handling of sensitive data because organisations can maintain full control over who sees what, at all times.
Engineered for the modern workplace
The 24B2D5300 also empowers the collaborative nature of modern workplaces. Two professionals can work together on either screen, either independently on the same task or project, or with one professional presenting to the other. The built-in 180-degree swivel in the base makes it possible to easily share either screen at any time.
True to modern standards, this Philips monitor is HDMI-ready and equipped with USB-C ports, with one dedicated to each screen. The USB-C connections support seamless device connectivity, fast data transfer, and up to 65 W power delivery on each port, as well as integrated USB hub and audio functionality. The panels on each screen are also engineered with Flicker-free and SoftBlue Technology with Low Blue Light panels and are Eyesafe Certified 2.0. Coupled with a fast refresh rate of 120 Hz, the dual-sided 24B2D5300 is not just easy to use but is also comfortable on the eyes.
Two users on one device as a space-saving solution
he Philips 24B2D5300's design features two screens, one on either side of the monitor. Each side can be connected to its own independent device via USB-C or HDMI, allowing two users to work simultaneously using separate input sources. Each screen can use MultiView, the Philips split view (picture in picture and picture by picture) technology and have the ability to work independently from each other. The compact design makes this monitor the ideal solution for workspaces which are short on space, not just in corporate environments, but for institutions such as libraries, universities, and schools. This dual device capability helps reduce the need for additional displays in shared environments.

articles.title: Este controlador te permite usar cualquier dispositivo con la lengua: se conecta por bluetooth y es un trackpad en tu paladar
articles.text:
Manejar el ratón de un ordenador con la lengua puede parecerte algo excéntrico. Pero más de 100 millones de personas con movilidad reducida no tienen tan fácil usar un ratón con sus manos, y es aquí donde entra, dispositivos como MouthPad^. Creado por la empresa estadounidense ^Augmental, se trata de un touchpad bucal para ordenadores, tablets y smartphones.
Se controla desde el paladar usando la lengua. Estamos ante un controlador bucal que te colocas en el paladar, y que pesa alrededor de 10 gramos. De hecho, se diseña a medida para poder tenerlo en la boca de forma cómoda. Una vez ahí, el controlador convierte los movimientos sutiles de la lengua y tu cabeza en movimientos de cursor, clicks, scrolling o movimiento de arrastrar elementos.
Su diseño es el de una férula transparente que se ajusta sobre los dientes superiores. Cuenta con un panel táctil sensible a la presión que se sitúa en el paladar, y unos sensores de movimiento para detectar los giros de la cabeza.
Su funcionamiento es muy sencillo.La lengua se mueve sobre el trackpad del paladar, y este movimiento mueve el cursor. También tiene un modo en el que lo que mueve el cursor son los movimientos de la cabeza. Entonces, igual que los trackpads que usas con la mano, una presión de la lengua equivale a un clic izquierdo, y un gesto de sorber al clic derecho. Todo lo demás es igual que usar un trackpad convencional, Puedes desplazar elementos, arrastrarlos y hacer casi lo mismo que en un panel táctil de un portátil.
Otra de sus características es que se conecta por Bluetooth como un ratón inalámbrico convencional. Esto permite que puedas usarlo en Windows, macOS, GNU/Linux, Android o iOS sin controladores adicionales ni configuraciones raras. Simplemente lo conectas y empiezas a hacer el movimiento con la lengua, es el propio dispositivo el que traduce tus movimientos para que los ordenadores y móviles lo entiendan.
Es igual que un ratón normal, conectar y empezar a usar. Es verdad que tiene aplicaciones oficiales para algunos sistemas que puedes descargar. Pero estas apps no son necesarias, simplemente sirven para configurar aspectos del control como la sensibilidad, velocidad del cursor o fuerza del clic.
Discreto y con buena autonomía. Otra de las principales características de este dispositivo es que es extremadamente discreto. Te lo colocas dentro de la boca donde no se puede ver, y tiene el mínimo impacto a la hora de hablar. Tiene un espesor de 1 milímetro, y está hecho de resina dental.
El controlador tiene unas dimensiones de aproximadamente 30 × 50 × 80 mm, y se carga mediante un cable USB-C a USB-A. El tiempo de carga completa es de 1,5 horas, y tiene una autonomía de más de 7 horas de uso continuo, con lo que te da casi para una jornada laboral.
No es el único dispositivo de este tipo. Ya en Xataka te hemos hablado de alternativas como el controlador MouthX creado en España, y que también te permite controlar cursores usando tu mandíbula y la lengua. Aquí, la diferencia es que MouthPad replica un trackpad de portátil con controles táctiles, mientras que la alternativa española replica dos joysticks.
De momento solo para Estados Unidos. La mala noticia es que este dispositivo de momento solo puede comprarse en Estados Unidos. La empresa sigue las regulaciones estadounidenses, pero no lo ha adaptado ni a las europeas ni a ningunas otras, por lo que solo hacen los envíos allí.
En cuanto al precio, ^Augmental cuesta 1.400 dólares, pero si compras dos se quedarán en 1.900 dólares por ambos. La clave está en que lo costoso es hacerlo a medida, y tras finalizar la compra la empresa te enviará instrucciones para compartirlas con tu dentista y hacerte un escaneo 3D de la boca que luego usarán para fabricar tu controlador.

articles.title: AI infrastructure systems power enterprise tech - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
AI infrastructure systems redefine the AMD-Nvidia rivalry as inference reshapes the market
The race to build AI infrastructure systems has moved beyond chip specifications into a battle over entire rack-scale platforms, as inference and agentic workloads redefine what counts as a computer.
That shift is forcing challengers, once judged purely on GPU benchmarks, to prove they can ship complete, integrated systems spanning compute, memory, networking, and software. Advanced Micro Devices Inc.’s five-year sprint to compress what took Nvidia Corp. 15 years to build shows how urgent that transformation has become, according to Dave Vellante (pictured, right), co-CEO of SiliconANGLE Media Inc. and co-host of theCUBE, SiliconANGLE Media’s livestreaming studio.
“They spent $60 billion in M&A, $49 billion of which was on Xilinx, and they seeded the ecosystem with software like ROCm,” Vellante said. “Now, to answer your question, they are now in the systems business. They’re no longer in just the chips business, and it’s a complete transformation and a reinvention. My premise is that they don’t have to take out Nvidia — they just have to become the essential second player, the second source in this AI wave.”
Vellante and John Furrier (left), co-founder and co-CEO of SiliconANGLE Media Inc. and co-host of theCUBE, held this conversation during theCUBE’s live coverage of AMD Advancing AI 2026, an exclusive broadcast on theCUBE, SiliconANGLE Media’s livestreaming studio. They unpacked AMD’s shift from chipmaker to systems provider and how inference, agentic workloads and enterprise economics are reordering AI infrastructure priorities. (* Disclosure below.)
AI infrastructure systems shift from chips to rack-scale platforms
Beyond hardware, the conversation increasingly centers on routing workloads to the right resource rather than defaulting to the most expensive silicon available. Enterprises are learning that not every task needs a frontier model or a top-tier GPU, Furrier noted.
“You start to see the software intelligence coming in to support the end-user, bottoms-up experience,” Furrier said. “This model goes to that CPU. It’s not that expensive, it’s not a high priority, but we need to have a good enough answer. Don’t use the expensive GPU for that — go to the right AI resource.”
AMD’s answer to that demand has been consolidating disparate acquisitions into a single systems narrative. Xilinx brought adaptive computing via field-programmable gate arrays, or FPGAs, while Pensando added DPUs and networking expertise as a critical part of the portfolio. That buildout has coincided with a broader climb in the data center business, as AMD’s rapid climb has written a new chapter of success that tech companies with its kind of longevity seldom see.
Still, Vellante cautioned that AMD and Nvidia are pursuing different philosophies even as both race toward rack-scale integration — one favoring tight, proprietary co-design and the other relying on openness and chiplets to win customers wary of lock-in.
“The winner will be whoever can, in the fastest way possible, redesign the entire computing experience around how humans actually think and work,” Furrier said. “Whoever gets there first, no one will care how it’s done.”

articles.title: MacBook OLED said to be on track for possible release later this year — but not everyone is excited
articles.text:
'Apple is entering 'the touchbar phase' again': MacBook OLED could be on track to launch in a few months, but skeptics still hate that rumored touchscreen
A touchy subject
- We just got a fresh info dump on Apple's incoming Macs from Bloomberg's Mark Gurman
- It includes the claim that the MacBook OLED may be on track for a debut later this year, and that it's now being tested with macOS 27.1
- The laptop would have the M5 Pro and Max chips, with a follow-up potentially arriving as early as the end of 2027 with the M7 Pro and Max
Apple will likely launch a whole load of new Macs over the next couple of years, and if you were wondering about the MacBook OLED, seemingly this laptop remains on target for a possible launch later this year.
Mark Gurman spilled a whole lot of info and updates in a Bloomberg report that details Apple's upcoming Mac overhauls, and how things stand right now (as ever, sprinkle seasoning on this liberally).
The model that many people are interested in is that MacBook OLED which will be a high-end effort in 14-inch and 16-inch sizes, sporting a touchscreen for the first time (not everyone's so keen on the latter, mind). They will pack the M5 Pro and M5 Max chips, not the M6.
Gurman says that this MacBook is currently being tested with macOS 27.1 by Apple, and that the device "remains on track for release between the end of this year and early next year". The leaker had previously asserted that we're looking at a late 2026 or early 2027 release (although there's a nuance here that I'll come back to shortly).
What about M6 MacBooks? We'll seemingly get a refresh of the low-end MacBook Pro 14-inch this year that packs the M6, and this will be the first launch to use the next-gen silicon. There will be new iMacs with the M6, too, all of which are supposedly arriving this fall (likely around October 2026, in other words, give or take a month).
The MacBook Air isn't being ignored, of course, and Gurman informs us that a refresh of this consumer lineup is coming in early 2027, with 13-inch and 15-inch models that "closely resemble the current version" — so don't expect much in the way of change.
Another MacBook Pro launch is, he says, planned for 2027 in the form of an entry-level 14-inch laptop with a new design that will be similar to the high-end OLED models, but this will have a major upgrade with the M7 (vanilla) chip.
Sign up for breaking news, reviews, opinion, top tech deals, and more.
Unsurprisingly, he adds that a refresh of the popular MacBook Neo is underway, which upgrades to an A19 Pro chip and offers more memory (new colors will be added, too).
Further down the line for MacBooks, there might be a more radical change coming for the MacBook Air, with an OLED take on the notebook that Gurman says could arrive in 2028, while a follow-up to the high-end MacBook OLED should debut between the end of 2027 and early 2028, with an upgrade from the M5 Pro and Max to the M7 Pro and Max.
Apple is also working on an iMac with OLED, Gurman believes, and we've heard about that before. (Much of this rumor dump is confirmation of previous speculation, it should be noted, with updates on timelines).
Gurman also tells us to expect refreshes in the realm of the Mac mini and Mac Studio. He claims the Mac mini is in testing with M5 Pro and M6 processors, while Apple looks to be going with the M5 Max and M5 Ultra for the Mac Studio. These would be trickier launches for Apple given the RAM crisis, and the need for beefier memory configurations causing additional headwinds for these particular Macs. Due to this, the launch timeframes for these purported products are, Gurman says, still up in the air.
Analysis: on track – but out of touch?
There's a lot in the pipeline, clearly, but the most interesting update here is that the high-end MacBook OLED is apparently still on target, and we could see it later this year – potentially in just a few months. Remember that not so long ago, Gurman appeared to waver on the idea of this touchscreen MacBook arriving in 2026 at all, but it seems that this is still very much in the cards (although not guaranteed, by any means).
This device is notably still missing a name, and the leaker isn't referring to it as the MacBook Ultra, as the broader rumor mill has been doing. That it packs the M5 Pro and M5 Max chips makes sense, because there will only be a vanilla version of the M6, according to what Gurman's heard on the grapevine before – Apple is apparently skipping swiftly over that generation to get to the M7 and more powerful AI capabilities therein. The follow-up to the high-end MacBook OLED will carry the Pro and Max chips from the M7 family, as noted.
In this report Gurman frames all these revamped Macs as Apple looking to "capitalize on demand for powerful laptops and desktops fueled by the artificial intelligence boom", underlining the recent emphasis the leaker has placed on how important AI is for Tim Cook's company now.
Predictably, this notion hasn't gone down well with some Mac fans, and the idea of a touchscreen on a MacBook (with that incoming OLED model) remains contentious, too, based on feedback from social media.
One Redditor puts it in particularly strong terms: "Touchscreen laptops are disgusting. I cannot fathom anyone actually using them. The ergonomics make no sense, the fingerprint factor is horrible, the OS is not built around touch the way tablets or phones are. Why are companies actively pursuing this technology in 2026?"
Another says: "Apple is entering 'the touchbar phase' again. Dark days lay ahead. I'll wait until they inevitably walk back whatever changes they make."
So, while people love the idea of an OLED, the fact that it's touch-capable is certainly dampening enthusiasm in some quarters, not forgetting that it'll add to the price tag, which is one of the other big fears about this laptop.

articles.title: OpenAI flambe : ses dépenses en IA explosent et atteignent 750 milliards de dollars, la pression est maximale
articles.text:
OpenAI vient de réviser son budget infrastructure à la hausse : 750 milliards de dollars d’ici à 2030, soit 25 % de plus que prévu il y a encore quelques mois. Un chiffre vertigineux qui, même en interne, commence à faire grincer des dents…
Désormais, la course à l’intelligence artificielle (IA) se joue surtout sur le terrain de la puissance de calcul. Et pour faire tourner des modèles toujours plus efficaces, OpenAI a besoin de data centers capables d’absorber une demande colossale. Une équation qui coûte de plus en plus cher, et que l’entreprise doit assumer en parallèle de sa préparation pour en entrer Bourse.
Car pour l’heure, le projet Stargate, annoncé en grande pompe début 2025 en partenariat avec Oracle et SoftBank, peine à décoller. Au pied du mur, la société de Sam Altman prend les choses en main et a décidé de construire ses propres centres de données.
Un premier data center made in OpenAI
Le premier chantier de cette nouvelle stratégie s’appelle le projet Camellia. Ce data center de 20 milliards de dollars doit voir le jour dans l’État de Géorgie, et puisera jusqu’à 3,2 gigawatts auprès du fournisseur local Georgia Power, une capacité qui devrait être pleinement disponible entre 2028 et 2032. En échange d’un abattement fiscal de 50 % pendant 15 ans, OpenAI s’engage à couvrir l’intégralité des coûts d’infrastructure et d’électricité.
Mais la frilosité en interne est palpable. Car les craintes des investisseurs sont bien là, et elles ne datent pas d’hier. En novembre 2025 déjà, Sam Altman annonçait 1 400 milliards de dollars de dépenses sur les 8 prochaines années. Dans la foulée, sa directrice financière Sarah Friar s’était alors empressée de rassurer discrètement les investisseurs en ramenant l’estimation à 600 milliards. C’est désormais officiel, cette somme atteint les 750 milliards de dollars, et est encore susceptible d’augmenter, note The Wall Street Journal.
- Chat dans différentes langues, dont le français
- Générer, traduire et obtenir un résumé de texte
- Générer, optimiser et corriger du code
Climat d’incertitude
En parallèle, une analyse du cabinet Emarketer publiée il y a quelques jours révélait qu’OpenAI allait rater ses objectifs de revenus publicitaires de près de 90 %. Il s’agit, pourtant, de l’un des leviers sur lesquels elle compte pour gonfler son chiffre d’affaires, alors même que sa grande concurrente, Anthropic, a récemment atteint la rentabilité.
À noter, en outre, que ce premier data center devrait être alimenté par du gaz naturel. Une situation qui n’est pas sans rappeler le cas de Colossus de SpaceXAI à Memphis, où les riverains se plaignent des dommages physiques et moraux de l’infrastructure.
D’ailleurs, OpenAI vient de recruter Brent Mayo, ancien responsable de la construction de Colossus, pour piloter ses propres chantiers.

articles.title: Giga Computing Accelerates Enterprise AI at Scale with 6th Gen AMD EPYC Server CPUs
articles.text:
Thursday, July 23rd 2026
	
		
	
	
	Giga Computing Accelerates Enterprise AI at Scale with 6th Gen AMD EPYC Server CPUs
Giga Computing, a subsidiary of GIGABYTE, is a global provider of advanced computing solutions that power the next generation of HPC, AI inference, 5G/edge, and cloud computing, today announced support for 6th Gen AMD EPYC Server CPUs across its server lineup, further expanding its portfolio of systems designed for demanding workloads. Now, at AMD Advancing AI 2026 in San Francisco, Giga Computing is debuting its first server for the new AMD EPYC 9006 platform.
Two Sockets, One Generation
With 6th Gen AMD EPYC Server CPUs, AMD introduces a two-socket strategy to serve the diverse workloads of the modern data center. The larger SP7 socket delivers leadership performance for the agentic AI era, with industry-leading memory bandwidth and PCIe Gen 6 connectivity, and the SP8 socket delivers efficient scale-out performance where density is the goal. Both sockets can be equipped with AMD performant "Zen6" or density "Zen6c" cores to fit the architecture of any deployment.Leadership Performance with SP7
AMD EPYC 9006 Server CPUs have up to 256 cores and 512 threads per socket, providing the density to run more virtual machines and AI services per rack while lowering overall TCO. PCIe Gen 6 connectivity and 16-channel DDR5 support provides the throughput to remove bottlenecks in networking and bandwidth. These features make SP7 the ideal processor for AI, HPC, hyperscale cloud, and telco 5G core deployments, where per-core performance and throughput matter most. For AI agents that need to run multiple workloads concurrently while maximizing GPU utilization, SP7 delivers the compute foundation to scale.
With SP7's compute density, Giga Computing can build rack-scale systems supporting over 40,000 CPU cores in a single liquid-cooled rack, giving agentic AI workloads the compute foundation to run multiple concurrent workflows, orchestrate GPU-fed pipelines, and scale enterprise AI deployments without compute bottlenecks. As autonomous agents take on increasingly complex, multi-step objectives, robust CPU infrastructure becomes essential to unlocking their full potential.
Scale-Out Efficiency with SP8
SP8 takes a different approach, delivering efficient compute for virtualization, database, and edge deployments where efficiency and consistency matter most. With a smaller footprint than AMD EPYC 9005 CPUs and greater performance per watt, the AMD EPYC 9006 processor SP8 socket is the perfect fit for power and space constrained environments. Despite the compact platform, SP8 offers 128 PCIe Gen 6 lanes and 2DPC memory support, delivering the I/O and memory flexibility enterprise workloads demand while maximizing performance per system dollar.
Platform Support for 6th Gen AMD EPYC Server CPUs
Across both SP7 and SP8, Giga Computing offers a comprehensive server portfolio that pairs each socket with the workloads it was designed for, spanning rack, blade, GPU, and edge systems. For the SP7 socket, several notable additions have been made to the GIGABYTE lineup. The new R165-DG2-CS1 is a single-socket rack server that uses closed-loop liquid cooling to support SP7's maximum 256-core configuration at max power within a 1U compact chassis. The B685-D80-LS1 is a 6U ten-node blade server with direct liquid cooling, purpose-built for high-density HPC deployments.
Shipments of GIGABYTE Servers, Powered by AMD EPYC 9006 Series Processors
9006 SP7 systems will begin shipments on day one along with AMD in November 2026. [SS1.1] 9006 SP8 systems will begin shipments in March 2027.
"AMD enterprise AI technologies have become the trusted foundation for the modern data center, and 6th Gen AMD EPYC Server CPUs extend that leadership with a new level of performance, efficiency and scalability," said Dan McNamara, senior vice president and general manager, Compute and Enterprise AI, AMD. "As enterprises scale cloud, HPC, virtualization and AI workloads, EPYC CPUs provide a trusted foundation for AI performance, infrastructure consolidation and innovation, while continuing to deliver leadership general-purpose compute for the business-critical applications and workloads that keep organizations running every day."
"Agentic AI and other enterprise AI deployments are placing incredible demands on data centers, driving the need for novel, more powerful solutions," said Daniel Hou, GM at Giga Computing. "Our new server platforms for AMD EPYC 9006 Series processors are engineered from the ground up, from board layout to power delivery to thermal design, so customers get GIGABYTE servers that are core-dense and space optimized without sacrificing performance. Whether it's for large-scale AI clusters or edge deployments, we've designed systems leveraging 6th Gen AMD EPYC Server CPUs that are ready from day one."
AMD Advancing AI
At AMD Advancing AI 2026, Giga Computing is showcasing the full breadth of its infrastructure portfolio, spanning server platforms advanced by AMD EPYC 9006 Series processors, and GIGABYTE systems built around the AMD Instinct MI350P and MI355X accelerators, AMD Pensando Pollara 400 AI NIC, and UfiSpace 800G switches. Together, these platforms deliver end-to-end AMD AI infrastructure, from host CPU to GPU accelerator, giving customers a validated foundation for AI deployments at scale.

These features make SP7 the ideal processor for AI, HPC, hyperscale cloud, and telco 5G core deployments, where per-core performance and throughput matter most. For AI agents that need to run multiple workloads concurrently while maximizing GPU utilization, SP7 delivers the compute foundation to scale.
With SP7's compute density, Giga Computing can build rack-scale systems supporting over 40,000 CPU cores in a single liquid-cooled rack, giving agentic AI workloads the compute foundation to run multiple concurrent workflows, orchestrate GPU-fed pipelines, and scale enterprise AI deployments without compute bottlenecks. As autonomous agents take on increasingly complex, multi-step objectives, robust CPU infrastructure becomes essential to unlocking their full potential.
Scale-Out Efficiency with SP8
SP8 takes a different approach, delivering efficient compute for virtualization, database, and edge deployments where efficiency and consistency matter most. With a smaller footprint than AMD EPYC 9005 CPUs and greater performance per watt, the AMD EPYC 9006 processor SP8 socket is the perfect fit for power and space constrained environments. Despite the compact platform, SP8 offers 128 PCIe Gen 6 lanes and 2DPC memory support, delivering the I/O and memory flexibility enterprise workloads demand while maximizing performance per system dollar.
Platform Support for 6th Gen AMD EPYC Server CPUs
Across both SP7 and SP8, Giga Computing offers a comprehensive server portfolio that pairs each socket with the workloads it was designed for, spanning rack, blade, GPU, and edge systems. For the SP7 socket, several notable additions have been made to the GIGABYTE lineup. The new R165-DG2-CS1 is a single-socket rack server that uses closed-loop liquid cooling to support SP7's maximum 256-core configuration at max power within a 1U compact chassis. The B685-D80-LS1 is a 6U ten-node blade server with direct liquid cooling, purpose-built for high-density HPC deployments.
Shipments of GIGABYTE Servers, Powered by AMD EPYC 9006 Series Processors
9006 SP7 systems will begin shipments on day one along with AMD in November 2026. [SS1.1] 9006 SP8 systems will begin shipments in March 2027.
"AMD enterprise AI technologies have become the trusted foundation for the modern data center, and 6th Gen AMD EPYC Server CPUs extend that leadership with a new level of performance, efficiency and scalability," said Dan McNamara, senior vice president and general manager, Compute and Enterprise AI, AMD. "As enterprises scale cloud, HPC, virtualization and AI workloads, EPYC CPUs provide a trusted foundation for AI performance, infrastructure consolidation and innovation, while continuing to deliver leadership general-purpose compute for the business-critical applications and workloads that keep organizations running every day."
"Agentic AI and other enterprise AI deployments are placing incredible demands on data centers, driving the need for novel, more powerful solutions," said Daniel Hou, GM at Giga Computing. "Our new server platforms for AMD EPYC 9006 Series processors are engineered from the ground up, from board layout to power delivery to thermal design, so customers get GIGABYTE servers that are core-dense and space optimized without sacrificing performance. Whether it's for large-scale AI clusters or edge deployments, we've designed systems leveraging 6th Gen AMD EPYC Server CPUs that are ready from day one."
AMD Advancing AI
At AMD Advancing AI 2026, Giga Computing is showcasing the full breadth of its infrastructure portfolio, spanning server platforms advanced by AMD EPYC 9006 Series processors, and GIGABYTE systems built around the AMD Instinct MI350P and MI355X accelerators, AMD Pensando Pollara 400 AI NIC, and UfiSpace 800G switches. Together, these platforms deliver end-to-end AMD AI infrastructure, from host CPU to GPU accelerator, giving customers a validated foundation for AI deployments at scale.

articles.title: On a testé la montre baroudeuse de Samsung : que vaut le pari de la finesse ?
articles.text:
| Taille boîtier | 47 mm | 
| Poids | 61.5 g | 
| Épaisseur | 10.7 mm | 
| Capteurs | Altimètre barométrique, Boussole, Cardiofréquencemètre, ECG, GNSS double fréquence, GPS, Profondimètre, SpO2 (oxygénation du sang), Température | 
| Profondeur maximale d'étanchéité | 100 m | 
| Solution de paiement | Oui | 
| Résolution | 327 ppp | 
| Technologie d'affichage | OLED | 
| Haut-parleur | Oui | 
| Compatible bracelet standard | Non | 
| Mémoire Interne | 64 Go | 
| Stockage musique | Oui | 
| Compatibilité | Android | 
| Système d'exploitation | Wear OS | 
Samsung renouvelle, deux ans après son premier modèle du genre, sa montre connectée dédiée aux sportifs exigeants. La Galaxy Watch Ultra 2 entend aujourd'hui faire mieux sur le plan du suivi sportif, des données de santé, de l'autonomie et de la robustesse. Tout un programme.
Deux ans après la Galaxy Watch Ultra première du nom, Samsung renouvelle une montre connectée destinée aux sportifs outdoor et pensée pour concurrencer l’incontournable alternative sous watchOS, l'Apple Watch Ultra. Son nouveau modèle Watch Ultra 2, facturé 750 €, se hisse sur un segment premium où pullulent les tocantes parfois très tournées vers la course à pied (Garmin Forerunner 970, par exemple), mais reste plus accessible que ses concurrentes directes, la Garmin Fenix 8 et l’Apple Watch Ultra 3.
Pour séduire, Samsung mise tout sur le suivi des activités en extérieur, mais aussi sur l’autonomie ; il faut dire que les tocantes sous Wear OS sont généralement à la peine sur le terrain de l’endurance. En exploitant la puce Snapdragon Wear Elite de Qualcomm et une nouvelle batterie à la capacité nettement augmentée, la Galaxy Watch Ultra 2 entend bien séduire les sportifs sur la durée.
Comme la première Watch Ultra, la Galaxy Watch Ultra 2 ne convient pas à tous les poignets. C’est une montre imposante, aux dimensions de boîtier presque identiques (47,4 x 47,1 mm) et tout aussi lourde (60,5 g). À titre de comparaison, ce boîtier pèse près du double de celui d’une Galaxy Watch 9 en 40 mm.
Néanmoins, la qualité de fabrication est au rendez-vous : le corps de la montre s’est affiné à 10,7 mm, tandis que celui de la première Watch Ultra dépassait les 12 mm. Il emploie du titane, gage de solidité, ainsi qu'un verre saphir pour protéger son écran Amoled de 1,5 pouce (498 × 498 pixels).
Ajoutons à cela une étanchéité à 10 ATM, une certification MIL-STD-810H (norme militaire dédiée à la résistance aux chocs, aux températures extrêmes, aux vibrations, etc.) et une estampille IP69K inédite chez Samsung, garantissant la résistance aux jets d'eau sous pression et à haute température : la Galaxy Watch Ultra 2 met toutes les chances de son côté pour séduire les baroudeurs.
C’est aussi cet écran qui interpelle. Pensée pour l’extérieur, la smartwatch annonce une luminosité maximale de 5000 cd/m², se hissant ainsi au sommet de notre comparatif. Nous l’avons éprouvée très largement en plein soleil sans rencontrer le moindre souci de lisibilité.
La luminosité de l’afficheur descend suffisamment bas pour ne pas gêner la nuit, et son fond d’écran s’ajuste automatiquement à la lumière ambiante. Ceux qui ne s'inquiètent pas pour l’autonomie de la batterie peuvent activer la fonction Always-on display (écran toujours allumé) pour un affichage permanent.
La Galaxy Watch Ultra 2 est flanquée d’un bracelet large de 22 mm, qui peut être remplacé, mais uniquement par un modèle à attache propriétaire. Par défaut, elle est livrée avec une version en silicone plutôt confortable, se fermant désormais par une boucle à ardillon ; le système utilisé auparavant (une boucle à glisser entre la peau et le bracelet) ne faisait vraisemblablement pas l’unanimité. Ce dernier, plus classique et sécurisant, peut être remplacé par des variantes en nylon ou en similicuir.
Précisons enfin que la Watch Ultra 2 est uniquement proposée en version Bluetooth et 4G, et qu’elle peut à ce titre accueillir une eSIM. Elle est compatible avec le Bluetooth 6.0 pour y connecter tous types d’écouteurs. Il est d’ailleurs possible de passer des appels au poignet grâce à l'intégration d’un haut-parleur convenable et d’un microphone. Côté capteurs, l'altimètre barométrique côtoie le profondimètre, le cardiofréquencemètre et le capteur de température cutanée.
La navigation est semblable à ce que proposent les autres Galaxy Watch. Sur le flanc droit de la montre, on retrouve trois boutons : le central, rond, n’est pas une couronne et n’accepte que l’appui. Une pression longue sur la touche supérieure (touche Accueil) convoque l’assistant vocal Gemini, tandis qu’un appui court permet de revenir au panneau d’accueil.
Un appui long sur le bouton inférieur (touche Retour) ouvre Samsung Wallet pour payer ses achats depuis la montre, tandis qu’une pression brève permet de revenir au panneau précédent. Au centre, la touche Rapide est dédiée au lancement d’une activité favorite. Toutes ces fonctionnalités peuvent être paramétrées depuis l’app Samsung Health pour répondre aux attentes spécifiques de chacun.
Le reste de la navigation passe par la dalle tactile. Balayez vers la gauche pour accéder aux notifications, puis vers la droite pour accéder aux widgets. Un mouvement de haut en bas fait apparaître les paramètres rapides, et l’inverse permet d’accéder aux apps installées sur la montre.
Les différents gestes habituels sont intégrés à la montre : il est possible de secouer le poignet, de pincer deux fois les doigts ou de “casser” le poignet deux fois pour réaliser des actions prédéterminées. À chacun de personnaliser tout cela dans l’application Samsung Health… une fois la montre appairée au smartphone via une seconde app, Galaxy Wear. La simplification attendra un peu.
La Galaxy Watch Ultra 2 s’appuie sur Wear OS 7 associé à One UI 9 côté montre, et sur la nouvelle mouture de Samsung Health côté smartphone. Cette app se veut capable d’offrir une vision que l’on pourrait qualifier d’holistique de la forme de l’utilisateur. Elle a gagné en fraîcheur du côté de l'interface, misant sur des couleurs douces, des graphiques et des indicateurs en tous genres. Avouons-le d’emblée : il faut vraiment prendre le temps de creuser pour exploiter (et même comprendre) les différents indicateurs mesurés par la montre. Samsung a fourni d’importants efforts, et cela se voit, pour mettre en perspective les données récoltées par sa montre. Pour l’utilisateur, il faut néanmoins un certain temps pour appréhender les nombreuses sections de l’application.
Cette app se décline en plusieurs panneaux : l’Accueil résume les différentes mesures réalisées par la montre ; Partage est un volet social, et Fitness inclut un nouvel indice (logiquement baptisé Indice Fitness), ainsi que des suggestions d’exercices vidéo destinés à l’améliorer. On note à ce titre que ceux de son partenaire iFIT sont payants, mais qu’une palette de vidéos YouTube gratuites est disponible.
Si tout cela paraît simple, c’est parce que nous n’avons pas détaillé l’Accueil, lui-même scindé en de multiples onglets. Exercice, Sommeil, Constantes, Pleine Conscience, Nutrition : tout y est. Vous pouvez obtenir un score de charge cardiaque, un score d’énergie, un score de sommeil, un indice Fitness… Si vous avez le tournis, c’est normal !
Quoi qu’il en soit, ceux qui souhaitent exploiter l’ensemble des fonctionnalités de la montre seront servis en données ultra-complètes. Ils peuvent même obtenir une évaluation de l’exposition aux environnements bruyants, pour prévenir d’éventuelles baisses d’audition !
La Watch Ultra 2 est estampillée Ultra, ce qui signifie qu'elle est autant pensée pour la santé que pour le sport. Elle se montre donc précise sur le plan du suivi du sommeil, assorti d'une mesure de la variabilité de la fréquence cardiaque (VFC), permet de réaliser des ECG au poignet, d'être alerté en cas de rythme cardiaque anormal ou encore de mesurer son index antioxydant.
Les personnes souhaitant suivre certains paramètres de santé spécifiques, les plus soucieuses de leur bien-être comme les amateurs de quantified self sont servis. La montre fait également appel à son capteur de température pour fournir un suivi du cycle menstruel aussi précis que possible.
Côté sport, la Watch Ultra 2 voit grand. Elle vise les sportifs du quotidien, évidemment, mais aussi les amateurs de pratiques plus intenses, sur terre ou sous l'eau. Pour ce dernier cas, Samsung propose moult certifications d'étanchéité, de l'IP69K au MIL-STD-810H, et surtout le support de la norme EN 13319 pour la plongée jusqu'à 40 m. Ce dernier point nous est difficile à vérifier (!), mais il reste à noter. Samsung s'est d’ailleurs fait accompagner d'un spécialiste du domaine, Mares, pour développer une app spécialement dédiée à la plongée, dont la disponibilité est prévue d'ici la fin de l'été 2026.
Les sportifs plus terre à terre peuvent profiter de nombreux modes d'activité, dont le plus intéressant est sans doute celui dédié au trail. La pratique est on ne peut plus tendance — d’après la dernière édition de l'Observatoire du running, quelque 74 % des coureurs (plus de 12 millions en France !) déclarent pratiquer le trail.
Il est donc logique que Samsung s'y mette et leur propose un mode incluant un accès à la cartographie en temps réel avec des alertes de dénivelé, des rappels d'hydratation et des écrans personnalisables en fonction des données biométriques que l'utilisateur souhaite afficher. On ne peut qu'apprécier l'initiative. Signalons que les récapitulatifs d'activités (quelles qu'elles soient) dans Samsung Health indiquent une estimation de la transpiration perdue et de la quantité d'eau à boire pour la compenser. La fonction existait déjà auparavant, mais s'avère bien davantage mise en avant dans cette dernière mouture.
Les coureurs sur route, chemins et autres circuits plus plats ne sont pas délaissés pour autant, puisqu’ils bénéficient d'un GPS double bande particulièrement efficace. Éprouvée en environnement urbain de notre côté, la Watch Ultra 2 (en bleu sur la cartographie ci-dessous) s'est révélée précise, malgré quelques légers écarts dans les zones les plus denses. La Watch GT Runner 2 de Huawei (en orange), pourtant elle-même précise habituellement, s'est visiblement emmêlé les fréquences le jour de cet essai, déraillant davantage que le modèle de Samsung.
Le module BioActive de Samsung n'a pas changé depuis la Galaxy Watch 8 et se montre convaincant. Testé lors de sessions d'endurance, il a suivi fidèlement notre fréquence cardiaque, malgré quelques rares décalages relevés ici et là. La courbe est régulière et la moyenne des écarts (0,53 bpm) témoigne de sa fiabilité.
En fractionné néanmoins, la précision s'est avérée moindre. Sur des blocs d'accélération assez classiques (50 s), on repère à la fois des écarts sur la fréquence maximale et des retards à la détection des pics. Rien de dramatique, mais on a vu plus précis ; la moyenne des différences avec notre ceinture pectorale de référence (Polar H10) dépasse en effet les 2 bpm.
Les mesures réalisées, notamment pendant la course, restent très nombreuses. Une estimation de la VO2max est livrée à l'issue de chaque session, tout comme une analyse de la posture et de la foulée. Le coach de running, inauguré sur la série Galaxy Watch 8 (qui propose des plans d'entraînement personnalisés pour préparer une course, d'un premier 5 km jusqu'au marathon), est toujours de la partie. Enfin, le mode dédié au cyclisme, lui aussi particulièrement riche en données, s'avère bien pensé.
La Galaxy Watch Ultra 2 est livrée avec son chargeur à induction habituel, promettant une charge rapide. Compte tenu de l'augmentation de la capacité de sa batterie, il n’est pas vraiment étonnant de constater que, malgré ses efforts, Samsung n’est pas parvenu à réduire le temps de charge : il faut compter presque 2 h 15 min pour faire un plein complet.
Fort heureusement, l’endurance de la montre s’est nettement améliorée par rapport à sa devancière, qui plafonnait à 2,5 jours selon notre protocole d’essai. Nous n’avons pas lésiné sur les activités sportives pour la mettre à l’épreuve : au terme d'une période de test de 48 h, incluant un peu plus de 5 h de vélo (avec des plages de pause) et 50 min de course à pied, le tout en conservant la gestion de nos notifications habituelles, nous sommes passés de 100 % à 37 %. Dans le cadre d’une utilisation plus classique, intégrant plusieurs sessions de course, nous avons relevé une autonomie de 3,3 jours. En se montrant plus économe sur le sport ou les notifications, on peut espérer flirter avec les quatre jours, mais pas davantage.
Samsung livre avec sa Galaxy Watch Ultra 2 une montre très complète. Elle s'adresse aussi bien aux sportifs les plus assidus, amateurs de pratiques outdoor (voire sous-marines), qu'à ceux qui souhaitent suivre au plus près un vaste panel d'indicateurs de santé, sans oublier les utilisateurs désireux de profiter de la richesse applicative de Wear OS sans se contenter d'une autonomie inférieure à deux jours. Il faut saluer les efforts fournis par le fabricant pour affiner sa Watch Ultra 2, la rendre plus robuste et améliorer son endurance. Néanmoins, mieux vaut ne pas espérer partir en vacances, voire en week-end, sans chargeur.
C'est la question du prix qui reste centrale ici. La Galaxy Watch Ultra de première génération demeure une bonne affaire, même si elle est moins robuste et endurante, son tarif ayant largement baissé au fil des mois. Les autres rivales de la montre connectée de Samsung, telle la Fenix 8 de Garmin, s'avèrent bien plus onéreuses, tout comme la Watch Ultra 3 d'Apple, réservée aux détenteurs d'iPhone.

articles.title: Cómo saber qué barra de sonido es la ideal para tu televisor y hogar
articles.text:
Frente a la limitación de los parlantes integrados en la mayoría de los televisores modernos, surge la necesidad de buscar alternativas que eleven la experiencia audiovisual y las barras de sonido suelen ser una de las primeras opciones por su facilidad de uso.
Sin embargo, elegir un dispositivo adecuado a las necesidades y las dimensiones del hogar es fundamental, para que el sonido se distribuya de la mejor manera posible, entregando la experiencia que estamos buscando.
PUBLICIDAD
Qué es una barra de sonido y cómo funciona
Una barra de sonido es un dispositivo compacto y alargado, diseñado para mejorar la calidad de audio de un televisor. Su función principal es ofrecer un sonido más claro, potente y envolvente que el que proporcionan los altavoces de fábrica.
Estas barras integran varios altavoces en su interior, como tweeters para las frecuencias agudas, altavoces medios para los diálogos y woofers para los graves. Al combinarse, logran crear un espacio sonoro más amplio y realista, capaz de resaltar tanto los diálogos como los efectos especiales de cualquier contenido.
PUBLICIDAD
Algunos modelos avanzados incorporan tecnologías como Dolby Atmos, que proyecta el sonido hacia el techo y las paredes para simular una experiencia tridimensional.
La instalación de una barra de sonido suele ser sencilla: basta con conectarla mediante HDMI ARC, óptico digital o incluso Bluetooth, según las opciones del televisor y la barra.
PUBLICIDAD
Tipos de barra de sonido según canales y tecnología
La cantidad de canales determina la complejidad y capacidad envolvente de una barra de sonido, según informes de marcas como Sonos y JBL. Las opciones más comunes son:
- 2.0: Dos altavoces (izquierda y derecha), que mejoran el estéreo básico.
- 2.1: Añaden un subwoofer para graves más potentes.
- 3.0 o 3.1: Incluyen un canal central que refuerza los diálogos, con o sin subwoofer.
- 5.1: Incorporan canales traseros y subwoofer, simulando el sonido envolvente clásico.
- 5.1.2 o 7.1.4: Modelos compatibles con Dolby Atmos, que agregan altavoces orientados al techo para un efecto tridimensional.
La elección del número de canales depende del tamaño de la sala y del tipo de contenido que más se consume. Para una experiencia cinematográfica inmersiva, los modelos con Dolby Atmos y canales de altura ofrecen una ventaja clara, mientras que para el uso diario en habitaciones pequeñas, una barra 2.1 puede ser suficiente.
PUBLICIDAD
Factores clave para elegir la barra de sonido adecuada
- Espacio disponible: la barra debe guardar proporción con el tamaño del televisor y el ambiente. En habitaciones pequeñas, modelos compactos optimizan el espacio, mientras que en salas amplias conviene invertir en barras más grandes y potentes.
- Compatibilidad y conectividad: verifica que la barra cuente con las entradas necesarias (HDMI ARC/eARC, óptico, Bluetooth, Wi-Fi). Los televisores más recientes suelen ser compatibles con HDMI eARC, que permite el máximo rendimiento de las tecnologías de sonido envolvente.
- Tipo de uso: quienes priorizan películas y series pueden preferir modelos con Dolby Atmos y subwoofer dedicado. Para videojuegos, es relevante la baja latencia y la posibilidad de conectar la consola directamente a la barra. En el caso de los aficionados a la música, conviene priorizar la calidad del procesamiento estéreo y las opciones de conectividad inalámbrica.
Consejos prácticos y errores comunes al elegir una barra de sonido
Un error frecuente es comprar una barra sin verificar la compatibilidad de entradas con el televisor, lo que puede limitar su uso o requerir adaptadores. Otro fallo habitual consiste en pensar que una barra económica ofrecerá siempre un sonido envolvente real, cuando en realidad la tecnología y la cantidad de canales son determinantes para este tipo de experiencia.
Empresas como Samsung advierten que la potencia, medida en watts, no es el único parámetro importante: la calidad del sonido y su adaptación al espacio son factores clave. Para habitaciones grandes, conviene priorizar modelos con subwoofer y, si es posible, parlantes traseros, mientras que en espacios pequeños basta con una barra compacta y eficiente.
PUBLICIDAD
La barra de sonido ideal es aquella que responde al uso cotidiano del hogar, se integra armónicamente con el televisor y el espacio, y satisface las expectativas de calidad de audio en función del presupuesto disponible.
Medir el espacio, revisar las especificaciones del televisor y tener claras las necesidades de uso son los pasos esenciales para elegir correctamente y transformar la experiencia frente a la pantalla.

articles.title: AMD’s new X100 chip lineup puts Strix Halo into robots – APUs for physical AI bring Zen 5 CPU, RDNA 3.5 GPU cores to compete with Intel’s Panther Lake
articles.text:
AMD’s new X100 chip lineup puts Strix Halo into robots – APUs for physical AI bring Zen 5 CPU, RDNA 3.5 GPU cores to compete with Intel’s Panther Lake
AMD takes on Intel (and Nvidia) in the robot wars.
AMD is bringing its Strix Halo APUs into the world of physical AI. The new X100 series of processors come with similar specs as the various Ryzen AI Max models floating around in client devices, but they’re tailored for 24/7 operation, with a 10-year lifecycle in embedded applications like robotics.
There are three SKUs that align with the three original Strix Halo models (not the updated versions with 40 CUs). The top-end X199 comes with 16 Zen 5 cores and 40 RDNA 3.5 CUs. The X188 steps down to 12 cores and 32 CUs, while the X168 comes with eight cores and the same 32 CUs. AMD hasn’t shared detailed specifications for each model, but the company says the range goes up to a 5.1 GHz boost clock and 128 GB of unified memory. They also include an XDNA 2 NPU with up to 50 TOPS, a configurable TDP between 45W and 120W, and operating temperature between -40 degrees Celsius up to 105 degrees.
AMD’s range bites back at Intel, which launched a range of Panther Lake SoCs for physical AI at the beginning of the year. Both make an argument for SoCs in robotics, reducing latency when the CPU, AI accelerator, and memory are fragmented across separate chips. The X100 range is just physically larger than Panther Lake, packing much more silicon on the SoC for more powerful deployments.
The company shared a range of benchmarks comparing the flagship X199 against Intel’s Core Ultra X7 358H, a 16-core chip with Intel’s Arc B390 iGPU that has 12 Xe3 cores. AMD claims a lead of 1.2X and 1.3X, respectively, in GeekBench 6.1 and PassMark, as well as 1.5X in an unofficial SPECrate 2017 run looking at integer workloads. In graphics, AMD unsurprisingly takes the edge with 1.4X faster Vulkan and 1.7X faster OpenGL performance (both measured with GFXBench 5 on Ubuntu), as well as a 1.6X lead in Unigine Heaven Extreme.
On the physical AI front, AMD claims a 1.4X improvement in Time to First Token (TTFT) and 3.5X faster tokens per second in Llama-bench, with a Vulkan backend running at a 45W TDP. These results need a massive dash of salt, however.
AMD tested the Ryzen AI Max 395+ “configured to reflect Ryzen AI Embedded X199 specifications.” It tested on the Maple reference board with a 5.1 GHz CPU clock, 2.9 GHz GPU clock, and sustained 45W TDP. The X7 358H, meanwhile, was tested in an MSI Prestige 16 Flip AI+ with an enforced TDP limit of 30W. AMD then “projected” 45W performance on the Intel chip “using scaling factors derived from public benchmark data.”
It’s not exactly an apples-to-apples comparison, in other words. There’s some sort of proxy stand-in or extrapolation of data across all of the benchmarks here, so keep that in mind as we work through the rest of AMD’s X100 announcements.
Get Tom's Hardware's best news and in-depth reviews, straight to your inbox.
AMD X100 Kria SOM and robotics developer platform
View Original
View Original
View Original
View Original
utside of the chips themselves, AMD is offering X100 models as part of a Kria System on Module (SOM) or an integrated robotics developer platform. The Kria X100 board measures 120mm x 120mm and conforms to the standardized COM-HPC form factor. If you’re a developer that wants to develop for the board, AMD is offering its Kria AI robotics developer platform.
It’s a fully-integrated box, leveraging the X100 Kria SOM alongside AMD’s Spartan UltraScale+ FPGA baseboard. AMD says it’s a “turnkey” solution for robotics development, including specialized connectivity for cameras and industrial networking, along with robotic sensors. The platform is available in early access now, and AMD says it’ll be in full production in Q4 of this year. .
AMD shared some benchmarks for the X100 Kria, as well, comparing it to Nvidia’s Thor T5000. These benchmarks weren’t run internally at AMD. They were commissioned by AMD and ran by Open Navigation and Mimix. Critically, the benchmarks didn’t test an X100 Kria board, or at least, not exactly in the form it will take once it’s inside a robot or AMD’s developer box.
Instead, AMD is comparing Nvidia’s Jetson AGX Thor developer kit to a GMKtech EVO-X2 AI mini PC with a Ryzen AI Max+ 395 “configured to reflect Ryzen AI embedded x199 specifications.” Naturally, the thermal and power environment of these chips will heavily influence performance.
View Original

View Original
AMD is continuing its attempt to siphon developers away from Nvidia’s CUDA platform for development, as well. It’s HIPIFY tool converts CUDA code to AMD’s HIP C++ portable code, and the company claims it can now handle 70-80% of the “effort” of porting on its own. AMD tested on a Ryzen AI Max+ 395, once again configured to match the X199, and it ported 15 CUDA applications, comprising 1,199 lines of code, to arrive at that 70% to 80% range.
X100 Kria lives at the “brain” of the robotics platform, but AMD envisions an end-to-end solution for humanoid-style robots with its Spartan UltraScale+. Zynq UltraScale+, and Versal AI Edge Gen 2 FPGAs and SoCs

articles.title: Agentic AI compute fuels AMD cloud infrastructure gains - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
Agentic AI compute reshapes cloud economics as AMD targets surging CPU demand
Agentic AI compute has become the defining workload of the cloud’s next era, reshaping how hyperscalers, neoclouds and enterprises architect their infrastructure. As autonomous agents move into production, demand for both GPUs and high-core-count CPUs is surging — and the economics of cloud computing are being rewritten in real time.
The shift echoes the cloud’s own explosive rise, but at a far faster pace. Advanced Micro Devices Inc. is positioning itself at the center of the shift with an open, full-stack approach designed to convert its cloud momentum into a durable advantage, according to Steve Berg (pictured), corporate vice president and general manager of the server CPU Cloud Business Group at AMD.
“It’s really been phenomenal to see what’s happened over even just the last — it’s not even 18 months that the agentic AI world has existed,” Berg said. “I’ve been doing this in the cloud for about 15 years, and watching the explosion that’s happening is amazing. The CPU is becoming much more relevant again — actually probably the most relevant element of the infrastructure in the agentic AI era today.”
Berg spoke with theCUBE’s John Furrier and Dave Vellante at AMD Advancing AI 2026, during an exclusive broadcast on theCUBE, SiliconANGLE Media’s livestreaming studio. They discussed how agentic AI compute is driving demand across cloud and hybrid infrastructure, AMD’s cloud market gains and the road to its next-generation EPYC “Venice” processors. (* Disclosure below.)
Agentic AI compute drives a heterogeneous hardware era
AMD’s rise in the cloud has been years in the making, built on a steady cadence of server chips that captured design wins from major providers. The company is targeting nearly 50% of the cloud CPU market on a revenue basis by year’s end, a goal it expects to reach through favorable total cost of ownership rather than raw specifications, Berg noted.
“The products have led to being able to win in the cloud world,” Berg said. “It’s a TCO play. It’s always a TCO play when it comes to cloud. And ensuring that they have the right performance per dollar for their workloads is how we’ve been able to become dominant in the cloud.”
That openness has helped AMD gain share even as hyperscalers design their own silicon. Enterprises want software compatibility across cloud, hybrid and on-premises environments without becoming locked into a single provider, Berg explained.
“It’s the enterprises that run in the cloud that want to have that open ecosystem, and they don’t want the lock-in,” he said. “They want to be able to run the same software and ecosystem that they do on-prem in a hybrid environment as they do in the cloud.”
The agentic era is fueling demand for a range of CPU configurations tailored to storage, high-performance computing and inference workloads, rather than a single processor for every use case, Berg noted. Those CPUs also handle orchestration, data routing and pre- and post-processing to keep expensive GPUs supplied with work. AMD’s forthcoming EPYC Venice processor, with up to 256 cores and a claimed 1.7-fold performance improvement, is built for these task-driven workloads, even as a tight memory market remains the biggest constraint on how fast the company can ship.
“Venice will be the best EPYC, will be the best agentic processor on the planet,” Berg said. “And I think everyone’s going to put it into their infrastructure to run agentic workloads.”

articles.title: "La vi en el cine y apenas llegué a los créditos": a Tarantino se le atragantó esta película que puedes recuperar en streaming
articles.text:
Quentin Tarantino lo admite sin monsergas: "la vi en el cine y apenas llegué a los créditos". Habla de 'Las amargas lágrimas de Petra von Kant', una de las películas de Rainer Werner Fassbinder que no logró ver entera (junto a 'Lili Marleen', que le pareció decepcionante). De toda la obra del alemán, cuarenta y cuatro películas entre 1969 y su muerte en 1982, dice haber visto solo cuatro. Tú puedes recuperarla en Filmin en una versión remasterizada, y en Movistar Plus.
'Petra von Kant' es justamente la pieza de cámara más citada de todas las películas de Fassbinder, rodada entera dentro del ático de una diseñadora de moda que se enamora de una modelo mucho más joven que ella y pierde el control sobre sus propios sentimientos. Margit Carstensen encarna a Petra con una teatralidad que le valió varios premios de la época, en un entorno opresivo y reforzado por un vestuario vanguardista y una espectacular fotografía de Michael Ballhaus.
Lo que distingue a la película es la distancia que impone entre el melodrama y el espectador: diálogos declamados con total ausencia de naturalismo, colores saturados hasta el artificio y una coreografía de cuerpos que deja a un lado todo rastro de espontaneidad. Directores como Olivier Assayas y Abel Ferrara la cuentan entre sus películas favoritas, pero a Tarantino se le atascó su estilo eminentemente europeo y el tono claustrofóbico que no sale del ático.
De todos modos, que nadie se espante: no es la primera vez que Tarantino se atraganta con una película aparentemente venerada: ya admitió que necesitó tres intentos para engancharse a 'Dunkirk', la película de Christopher Nolan que acabó convirtiéndose en la que defiende con más pasión. Es lo que tiene el cine que funciona como un asalto a los sentidos: no necesariamente tiene que entrar fácil.
