articles.title: Startup news and updates: daily roundup (July 23, 2026)
articles.text:
Startup news and updates: daily roundup (July 23, 2026)
YourStory presents the daily news roundup from the Indian startup ecosystem and beyond. Here's the roundup for Thursday, July 23, 2026.
Community agriculture is the way forward for farmers to enhance their livelihoods even as Indian startups continue to raise funding, YourStory brings you today’s headlines with the latest developments across sectors
This woman entrepreneur is helping small farmers earn more through community-supported agriculture
Spudnik Farms, founded by Sumeet Kaur, connects urban consumers with local farmers through a subscription model. The company works with 250 farmers across Karnataka, helping them earn higher incomes while promoting seasonal, indigenous and sustainably grown produce.
Funding news
Banking tech company BusinessNext raises $40M from ServiceNow
Workplace management software company ServiceNow has announced an investment of $40 million in BusinessNext, a Noida-headquartered technology firm focused on banking and financial services industry. The Series C round has valued BusinessNext at $700 million and is aimed at strengthening the company's efforts to drive autonomous operations and private AI solutions across banking and financial services.
Tech30 startup CARPL.ai raises $10M in Series A led by IFC
CARPL.ai, a radiology AI marketplace and enterprise platform, has raised $10 million in a Series A round of funding led by International Finance Corporation (IFC), the private sector arm of the World Bank Group, with participation from Stellaris Venture Partners and other investors. CARPL.ai was part of the YourStory Tech30 cohort of 2022.
Farm Watt Innovations raises Rs 32.5 Cr to expand bioenergy network
Farm Watt Innovations has raised Rs 32.5 crore in a funding round co-led by IAN Alpha Fund and Rainmatter to strengthen India's bioenergy supply chain. The climate-focused agribusiness converts agricultural waste into biomass for compressed biogas (CBG) plants and other renewable energy applications, helping reduce stubble burning and greenhouse gas emissions while creating rural livelihoods.
The fresh capital will be used to expand biomass collection networks, establish additional aggregation hubs, invest in machinery and strengthen its workforce. Going forward, the company plans to develop its own portfolio of CBG, bio-pellet and biochar plants, creating an integrated circular bioeconomy platform that delivers environmental, social and economic benefits.
Wiffy secures $3 million Series A funding
Home improvement services platform Wiffy has raised $3 million in a Series A funding round led by Earth Fund, with participation from Persol Holdings of Japan and existing investor Capria Ventures. The company provides post-sales installation and maintenance services for more than 100 brands, including IKEA, Panasonic, Godrej, Hettich and Amazon.
The proceeds will be used to enhance its technology platform, strengthen AI-powered workforce management, expand enterprise partnerships and enter new service categories. Wiffy operates through a network of over 5,000 certified technicians and has served more than one million homes across 100 cities, while maintaining a business model driven primarily by enterprise partnerships.
NeuralKart raises Rs 2.35 Cr in seed funding
AI-powered insurtech startup NeuralKart has raised Rs 2.35 crore in a seed funding round led by Inflection Point Ventures. The Bengaluru-based company develops AI-driven decision-making tools that automate insurance underwriting, claims processing and industrial safety assessments. The fresh capital will be used to strengthen product development, expand AI and machine learning capabilities, and accelerate customer acquisition and go-to-market initiatives.
NeuralKart said it has already secured paying enterprise customers and maintains a 100% customer retention rate. The company works with leading insurers and industrial risk services firms and has also entered into a co-development partnership for its FieldSense platform, targeting the growing insurance automation and industrial safety technology markets.
Upkraft secures Rs 1.6 Cr in pre-seed round
AI-powered extracurricular learning platform Upkraft has raised Rs 1.6 crore in a pre-seed funding round led by PedalStart, with participation from angel investors, entrepreneurs and early-stage ecosystem players. Founded by Tejasvi Singh Kushwah, Varun Mangal and Kritika Varandani, the startup offers structured extracurricular learning programmes for students at homes, schools and residential communities.
The company will use the proceeds to develop AI-powered personalised learning tools, expand operations across Bengaluru and Gurugram, strengthen its technology platform and build teams across product, engineering, sales and tutor operations. Over the next 12 to 18 months, Upkraft aims to increase student enrolments and deepen its presence in key markets.
Other news
Utho Cloud to deploy 10,000 GPUs for sovereign AI
Utho Cloud has announced plans to deploy 10,000 GPUs over the next seven to eight quarters to strengthen India's sovereign AI infrastructure. The investment will include NVIDIA's H200, H100, A100, RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell and L4 GPUs, enabling enterprises, startups, researchers and government organisations to access high-performance AI computing hosted entirely within India.
The company said its platform will offer predictable pricing in Indian rupees, guaranteed GPU availability, data residency compliant with the Digital Personal Data Protection Act and 24x7 support. With more than 51,000 users, Utho aims to reduce dependence on overseas cloud infrastructure while providing secure AI computing capabilities for domestic organisations.
Google concludes Build with AI parliamentary showcase
Google has concluded the Parliamentary Showcase of its Build with AI: Code for Communities programme, an initiative aimed at connecting AI innovation with public governance. Organised with The Dialogue, the programme saw 12 winning developer teams present AI-powered solutions before Members of Parliament.
More than 7,000 developers from over 18 Indian cities participated, creating over 1,000 open-source projects using Google's Gemini and Gemma AI models. The solutions addressed civic governance, public health, agriculture and environmental challenges. Google said selected projects will now be piloted in parliamentary constituencies, demonstrating how AI can be used to improve public service delivery and community welfare across the country.
Cars24 Labs partners Startup Policy Forum on AI
Cars24 Labs, the AI innovation arm of Cars24, has partnered with the Startup Policy Forum (SPF) to support responsible AI adoption and policy development in India. Under the partnership, Cars24 Labs will contribute to AI policy discussions, founder engagements, industry dialogues and global immersion programmes while sharing practical insights from deploying AI across its business. SPF represents more than 75 new-age companies and works to strengthen India's startup ecosystem. The collaboration aims to bring together founders, policymakers, researchers and technology leaders to exchange ideas and help shape AI policy. Cars24 Labs said the initiative reflects its commitment to supporting India's emergence as a global leader in artificial intelligence.
Cashfree Payments waives gateway fees for new merchants
Cashfree Payments has introduced a limited-period offer waiving payment gateway charges for new businesses on the first Rs 20 lakh of gross merchandise value (GMV) processed through its platform until March 31, 2027. The initiative is aimed at helping small and growing businesses improve cash flow ahead of the festive season. Besides the fee waiver, new merchants will benefit from onboarding within minutes, next-day settlements and dedicated account managers during the peak sales period. Cashfree said the move will allow businesses to reinvest savings into inventory, marketing and logistics while simplifying digital payments and reducing operational costs for small and medium enterprises.
Wipro Consumer Care acquires Good Home and Eva brands
Wipro Consumer Care & Lighting has signed definitive agreements to acquire the Good Home and Eva brands from TTK Healthcare Ltd. for Rs 256 crore. The acquisition strengthens Wipro's presence in the home care and personal care segments. Good Home offers products including air fresheners, scrubbers and drain cleaners, while Eva is among India's established deodorant brands with body sprays, perfumes, roll-ons and talcum powders. Together, the two brands generated Rs 148 crore in revenue during FY26. Wipro said the acquisition aligns with its strategy of expanding into trusted, high-growth consumer categories driven by rising hygiene awareness, premiumisation and evolving lifestyle preferences.
Campus Fund appoints Howard Morgan to advisory board
Campus Fund, a venture capital firm focused on student- and dropout-led startups, has appointed veteran investor Dr. Howard L. Morgan to its Global Advisory Board. Morgan is Chair and General Partner at B Capital and co-founder of First Round Capital, an early investor in companies including Uber, Square, Roblox and Notion. His appointment comes as Campus Fund deploys its third and largest fund— a $100 million corpus announced in June 2025 — to support up to 60 startups over four years. The fund evaluates more than 7,000 startups annually through a network of over 100 student scouts, with investments spanning deeptech, space technology and climate technology.
Quest Global named leader in ISG semiconductor study
Engineering services firm Quest Global has been recognised as a Leader in the ISG Provider Lens Semiconductor Industry Services and Solutions 2026 Study for the US market. The company earned leadership positions in Design, Test and Verification Services and Manufacturing and Engineering Services. ISG highlighted Quest Global's capabilities across silicon engineering, custom SoC and ASIC development, embedded systems and manufacturing engineering. The report also recognised the company's "Silicon to Systems to Cloud" approach and AI-enabled engineering methodologies, which help semiconductor companies reduce design cycles, improve first-pass silicon success and accelerate the development of next-generation semiconductor products.
InCred Asset Management crosses Rs 1,000 crore healthcare AUM
InCred Asset Management has crossed Rs 1,000 crore in investments across listed healthcare companies through its portfolio management services, becoming one of India's largest dedicated healthcare PMS providers. Launched in February 2021, the healthcare strategy has delivered a 18.97% CAGR, outperforming the BSE 500 TRI's 13.27% CAGR, according to the company. The portfolios invest across pharmaceuticals, hospitals, diagnostics, medical technology and contract research businesses. InCred said the milestone reflects growing investor confidence in India's healthcare sector, supported by structural factors such as rising healthcare spending, expanding insurance coverage, favourable demographics and increasing innovation in healthcare services.
Konnect Insights launches AI-powered Research Cloud
Customer experience platform Konnect Insights has launched Konnect Research Cloud (KRC), an AI-powered intelligence platform designed to help enterprises analyse customer data across multiple systems using natural language queries. The platform connects with existing customer-facing technology stacks and delivers evidence-backed insights in seconds to support business decision-making. KRC marks the first step towards the company's vision of building a Front Office Operating System that unifies enterprise technologies through AI. The solution is immediately available to enterprise customers worldwide. Konnect Insights operates cloud infrastructure across India, the UAE, Saudi Arabia, the US, the UK and Germany to ensure compliance with regional data residency requirements.
PhysicsWallah partners NWWA to support Navy families
Education company PhysicsWallah (PW) has signed a memorandum of understanding with the Indian Navy Welfare & Wellness Association (NWWA) to provide educational support to the families of Indian Navy personnel. Under the initiative, families of Navy martyrs and personnel who died during service will receive full scholarships, while serving and retired personnel's families will be eligible for discounts on PW's offline coaching and online courses. The scholarships cover preparation for competitive examinations including JEE, NEET, UPSC, SSC CGL and state public service commissions. Applications will be jointly verified by NWWA and PW, with the programme aimed at making quality education more accessible to defence families across India.
FincFriends reports 43% growth in assets under management
Digital lending NBFC FincFriends reported a 43% year-on-year increase in assets under management to Rs 875 crore in FY26, while revenue rose 33% to Rs 999 crore. Loan disbursements during the year climbed to Rs 3,732 crore, compared with Rs 2,585 crore in the previous fiscal. The company said it has served more than 5.5 million borrowers since inception and currently processes around 3,000 digital loans every day. Looking ahead, FincFriends plans to expand its customer base, strengthen partnerships, improve portfolio quality and grow its near-prime lending business through higher-ticket loans, supported by a profitable business model and strong institutional backing.
Workday launches AI-powered learning platform with Sana
Workday has announced the general availability of Workday Learning, powered by Sana, an AI-driven learning solution designed to deliver personalised employee training. The platform combines Workday's workforce and skills data with Sana's AI capabilities to provide tailored learning recommendations, AI tutoring and automated course creation. Administrators can also use AI to streamline assignments and learning campaigns, reducing manual effort. The integrated solution is now available globally for Workday Human Capital Management customers, while Sana Learn will also be offered as a standalone product for organisations not using Workday's HR or financial management platforms.
StraitsMicro unveils sovereign surveillance chip family
Singapore-based StraitsMicro has unveiled Visora, a sovereign camera System-on-Chip (SoC) family designed as an indigenous alternative for surveillance systems following India's restrictions on Chinese surveillance chips. The new semiconductor platform is aimed at government, defence, smart city and critical infrastructure applications in India and overseas. Developed with Bengaluru-based design partner Proxelera and distributor Aqtronics, Visora features AI acceleration, low-power multicore processors, advanced video compression and edge AI capabilities including facial recognition, crowd analytics and behavioural analysis. The company said the platform supports India's drive towards secure, locally developed semiconductor technologies for surveillance infrastructure.
Bijliride expands student EV rental programme
Electric mobility platform Bijliride has expanded its Project Udaan initiative by launching a student-focused electric two-wheeler rental programme across major Indian cities. The scheme offers flexible, zero-commitment EV rentals while integrating optional micro-gig delivery opportunities that allow students to offset their daily rental costs. The company said the initiative addresses commuting challenges and promotes financial independence without requiring long working hours. Bijliride has reported steady growth in registrations across Hyderabad, Pune, Bengaluru, Mumbai and Delhi-NCR, with students using the vehicles for internships, examinations and skill development programmes. The company believes the initiative will encourage sustainable mobility and increase electric vehicle adoption among young consumers.
Enmovil appoints Jayaraman Krishnamurthy as global sales head
AI-native supply chain orchestration platform Enmovil Solutions has appointed Jayaraman Krishnamurthy as its Head of Global Sales to drive international expansion across India, the US and the Asia-Pacific region. Krishnamurthy brings over 25 years of experience in enterprise software, manufacturing and supply chain, having held leadership roles at Asian Paints, SAP, Capillary Technologies and o9 Solutions. In his new role, he will lead the company's global sales strategy and strengthen its presence in key international markets. Enmovil said the appointment comes as manufacturers increasingly adopt digital supply chain solutions, positioning the company to capitalise on growing global demand for AI-driven supply chain intelligence platforms.
ePlane, Apollo Hospitals partner on electric air ambulances
The ePlane Company and Apollo Hospitals Enterprise Ltd. have signed a memorandum of understanding to introduce electric air ambulances and medical delivery drones into India's emergency healthcare network. Under the partnership, ePlane's e200X aircraft will be deployed for rapid inter-hospital patient transfers, trauma care, cardiac emergencies and organ transport, while its subsidiary Amber Wings will provide drones for transporting blood, medicines, vaccines and diagnostic samples.
Apollo will explore potential orders for the aircraft and drones and may consider a strategic investment in ePlane. The companies will also work with aviation regulators to develop the infrastructure needed for advanced air mobility in healthcare.
Vertiv names Raghavendra Kale India channel leader
Critical digital infrastructure provider Vertiv has promoted Raghavendra Kale as its Channel Leader for India. In his new role, Kale will lead the company's channel sales strategy, expand its partner ecosystem and strengthen engagement across key reseller and distribution segments. He previously served as Director, West Zone, Channel, where he played a key role in improving operations and driving business growth. With nearly three decades of industry experience, Kale is expected to help scale Vertiv's partner-led business strategy while nurturing strategic accounts and expanding the company's market reach in India amid growing demand for digital infrastructure solutions.
BULLET appoints Apurba Sen as VP, Business Strategy & Sales
Microdrama platform BULLET, backed by ZEE Entertainment Enterprises, has appointed Apurba Sen as Vice President, Business Strategy & Sales. The appointment comes after the launch of Trinetra AI, the company's AI-powered filmmaking and content intelligence platform.
Sen will oversee strategic initiatives across BULLET Microdrama, Trinetra AI and future business ventures, focusing on partnerships, fundraising, commercial expansion and international growth. He brings more than two decades of experience in advertising technology, streaming, connected TV, AI-driven creative technologies and digital platforms. The company said the appointment strengthens its leadership team as it expands its AI-enabled entertainment ecosystem.

articles.title: "Nous avons assurément des projets” : Kevin Feige confirme l'arrivée imminente de Miles Morales dans le MCU
articles.text:
"Nous avons assurément des projets” : Kevin Feige confirme l'arrivée imminente de Miles Morales dans le MCU
Alors que Spider-Man : Brand New Day s'apprête à déferler sur les écrans de cinéma mondiaux, Kevin Feige, le grand manitou de l'univers cinématographique Marvel, a dévoilé que l'arrivée de Miles Morales n'était qu'une question de temps.
Les fans de l'homme-araignée peuvent être contents : Spider-Man : Brand New Day arrive au cinéma ce 29 juillet prochain, le film d'animation Spider-Man: Beyond the Spider-Verse est lui prévu pour dans moins d'un an, et même la récente série Spider-Noir de Prime Video est une franche réussite.
Et pour contribuer à la fête, le patron du MCU Kevin Feige vient tout juste de confirmer en interview que Marvel et Sony travaillent sur une arrivée prochaine du populaire Miles Morales dans l'Univers Cinématographique Marvel.
Un Miles Morales en live action dans les tuyaux
Dans une interview accordée au site chinois Watching Hollywood, et relayée par nos confrères américains du site Deadline, Kevin Feige a en effet confirmé qu'une version en live action de Miles Morales était définitivement prévue :
"Oui, nous avons assurément des projets, et je pense qu’un film Spider-Man en prises de vues réelles est voué à intégrer Miles, quelque temps après la conclusion de la saga Spider-Verse."
Feige ajoute : "Nous réfléchissons et discutons de nouvelles aventures de Spider-Man, indépendamment des accords ou des contrats. Ma partenaire de production, Amy Pascal, y travaille déjà, et nous avons eu des discussions approfondies sur ce que pourraient raconter les deux, trois, quatre et cinq prochains films Spider-Man."
Pour rappel, Miles Morales et un variant de Spider-Man créé par Brian Michael Bendis et Sara Pichelli et apparu pour la première fois dans les comics en 2011. Sa popularité l'a amené en 2018 à devenir le héros du film d'animation Spider-Man : New Generation (ou Into the Spider-verse en VO) qui a conquis les spectateurs et remporté l'Oscar du meilleur film d'animation.
Sa suite sortie en 2023, Across the Spider-Verse, a elle aussi connu un succès public et critique, générant près de 700 millions de dollars au box-office mondial. Un troisième film, Beyond the Spider-Verse, est lui attendu le 23 juin 2027 au cinéma. Il a de plus était le héros des jeux vidéo Spider-Man d'Insomniac Games.
Cette confirmation claire comme de l'eau de roche de Kevin Feige devrait donc réjouir les fans, alors qu'une arrivée de Miles Morales en chair et en os dans l'Univers Marvel était suggérée depuis de longues années. Dans Spider-Man : No Way Home, le personnage d'Electro (joué par Jamie Foxx) disait ainsi "Il doit bien avoir quelque part un Spider-Man noir" au détour d'un dialogue.
Enfin, cette déclaration de Kevin Feige corrobore les propos tenus par Amy Pascal, la productrice historique des films Spider-Man, qui disait déjà en 2023 qu'un film live action autour de Miles Morales était en développement.
Alors que Spider-Man : Brand New Day devrait déjà apporter son lot de réponses, les fans devraient avoir nettement plus d'informations concernant l'avenir du MCU dès la semaine prochaine lors du Comic Con de San Diego. À suivre donc.

articles.title: Gratuit, ce logiciel peut rendre votre clavier beaucoup plus intelligent
articles.text:
L'adresse postale, la formule de politesse, le paragraphe d'explication envoyé dix fois par semaine : une partie de votre clavier tourne en boucle. Espanso remplace ces litanies par des raccourcis de quelques caractères, gratuitement.
Le principe de l'expansion de texte rappelle la correction automatique du smartphone, à ceci près que le dictionnaire, c'est vous qui l'écrivez. Espanso, créé par le développeur italien Federico Terzi et aujourd'hui maintenu par une petite équipe, applique la recette à tout le système, sous Windows comme sur macOS et Linux. Publié sous licence libre GPL-3, le logiciel bénéficie toujours d'un développement actif avec une version 2.3 publiée en octobre 2025.
Deux points, quatre lettres, et le paragraphe s'écrit tout seul
Tout repose sur des déclencheurs : tapez « :mail » dans n'importe quelle application (messagerie, navigateur, traitement de texte) et Espanso substitue instantanément le texte associé, sans copier-coller. Les correspondances se rangent dans de simples fichiers texte au format YAML, qui se lisent comme des fiches de recettes : à gauche l'abréviation, à droite le texte servi.
- Open source
- Très personnalisable
- Fonctionne partout
Le logiciel dépasse le bloc de texte figé. Des variables insèrent la date du jour ou le contenu du presse-papiers, des formulaires ouvrent une petite fenêtre à compléter avant de générer la réponse, et des déclencheurs à motifs gèrent les cas plus fins. Les bricoleurs peuvent même injecter le résultat d'un script ou d'une commande directement dans leur texte. Une barre de recherche, appelée par Alt+Espace, retrouve le bon extrait quand la mémoire flanche.
Pour ne pas partir d'une page blanche, le Hub d'Espanso propose des paquets communautaires prêts à l'emploi : émojis, caractères accentués, extraits de code ou gabarits de réponses s'installent en une commande.
Zéro abonnement, zéro cloud, et un code que chacun peut lire
La référence commerciale du secteur, TextExpander, facture 3,33 dollars par mois (environ 40 dollars à l'année) pour l'essentiel de ce qu'Espanso offre gratuitement à un utilisateur seul. L'écart se justifie surtout pour les équipes, à qui l'outil payant apporte partage de bibliothèques et administration centralisée ; en solo, la note s'arrête à zéro.
La confidentialité pèse tout autant dans la balance. Un outil d'expansion de texte, par construction, surveille la frappe pour repérer ses déclencheurs : mieux vaut savoir qui regarde. Ici, tout s'exécute et se stocke en local, sans compte ni synchronisation imposée, le code ouvert se laisse auditer, et les binaires Windows sont signés numériquement. La contrepartie assume son public : la configuration passe par des fichiers texte, sans interface graphique d'édition, ce qui ravira les habitués des éditeurs de code et rebutera les allergiques.

articles.title: Gaming wird teurer: Vom Verschwinden physischer Medien und den Absichten der großen Hersteller
articles.text:
Gaming ohne physische Medien: Wieso es für Gamer teurer wird – und diese Entwicklung kein Zufall ist
Die Nachricht kam plötzlich und war trotzdem abzusehen: Per Blog-Post verkündete Playstation, kürzlich dass neue Spiele ab Januar 2028 nicht mehr auf Discs veröffentlicht werden. Es ist also davon auszugehen, dass die Playstation 6 schon ohne Disc-Laufwerk hergestellt wird. Stattdessen sollen Games nur noch über den Playstation Store und in digitaler Form im Einzelhandel erhältlich sein.
Dies sei für das Unternehmen ein „natürlicher Schritt, um sich an die Verbrauchertrends anzupassen, da die allgemeine Nachfrage nach digitalen Medien die nach physischen Datenträgern mittlerweile deutlich übersteigt“. Das ist durchaus richtig. So liegt der Anteil an digitalen Verkäufen bei Herstellern inzwischen teils bei über 90 Prozent. Dennoch dürfte dieser Schritt für viele Gamer teuer werden – und das ist kein Zufall.
Eigentlich nichts Neues – aber!
Wer auf dem PC spielt, kennt diesen Umstand schon lange. Hier ist es nichts Neues, dass Games allein in digitaler Form verkauft werden. Der Großteil davon über die Verkaufsplattform Steam. Doch es gibt einen großen Unterschied zu einem Ökosystem wie der Playstation: auf dem PC hat man die freie Wahl.
Sicherlich ist Steam die wichtigste Plattform für alle großen Entwicklerstudios. Wer mit seinem Spiel Erfolg haben will, muss hier präsent sein. Aber es gibt eben doch Alternativen. Vom Epic Games Store bis zu GOG: Gamer können auf dem PC entscheiden, wo sie ihr Spiel kaufen wollen. Und damit etwa auch Rabatte wahrnehmen, die in einem Store angeboten werden und im anderen nicht.
Wer ab 2028 sein digitales Spiel auf der Playstation kaufen möchte, hat diese Möglichkeit nicht. Die Ökosysteme der Hersteller Playstation, Xbox und Nintendo basieren darauf, dass auf ihren Konsolen nur die eigenen Verkaufsplattformen genutzt werden können. Sie allein bestimmen die Preise, Alternativen gibt es nicht.
Für die Hersteller ist das freilich sehr lukrativ. Zumal sie, anders als etwa auf dem PC, keine Abgaben an eine Plattform wie Steam zahlen müssen. Die Erlöse über den Playstation Store gehen bei den eigenen Spielen allein an Sony. Der Schritt hin zum rein Digitalen ist für das Unternehmen also ein monetär äußerst vorteilhafter.
Keine Spiele, sondern Lizenzen
Für die Gamer aber sieht es anders aus. Wo es keine Auswahl und Konkurrenz gibt, gibt es auch nur selten günstige Preise. Ein Vergleich wie auf dem PC ist nicht möglich. Zudem ermöglichen Plattformen wie GOG einen DRM-freien Kauf. Das heißt, dass Spiele ohne Kopierschutz verkauft werden, der oft eine konstante Online-Verbindung voraussetzt. Wer hier ein digitales Spiel kauft und es auf einer Festplatte speichert, kann davon ausgehen, es auch in vielen Jahren noch spielen zu können.
Auf Konsolen sieht das anders aus. Wer etwa im Playstation Store ein Spiel kauft, der erwirbt, wie auf jeder digitalen Verkaufsplattform, auch eine Lizenz – die theoretisch aber auch wieder entzogen werden kann. Doch sind diese Lizenzen hier immer an den Account gebunden. Und wenn der gesperrt wird, ist kein Zugang zum Spiel mehr möglich. Erst kürzlich machte Playstation zudem damit Schlagzeilen, dass das Unternehmen um die 500 Inhalte aus seinem Store gelöscht hat. In diesem Fall handelte es sich um Filme, die nun nicht mehr gestreamt werden können – auch wenn sie käuflich erworben wurden.
Schon seit Jahren bewegt sich die gesamte Industrie immer mehr in Richtung sogenannter Service-Games. Spiele also, die nur online gespielt werden können und darauf ausgelegt sind, dass Gamer sie über Monate, wenn nicht Jahre, spielen. Mit kontinuierlichen Updates und neuem Content. Doch wenn das Spiel nicht erfolgreich ist, werden die Server abgestellt – und das Spiel wird unbrauchbar.
In einer Zukunft ohne physische Spiele und digitalen Games, die nur noch auf hauseigenen Plattformen angeboten werden, wird dieses Risiko nochmal größer. Denn dann könnte selbst das bereits gekaufte Singleplayer-Game nicht mehr funktionieren, wenn es aus dem digitalen Geschäft verschwindet oder der eigene Account nicht mehr aktiv ist. Und auch das kann für die Hersteller lukrativ sein. Ältere Services, die kein oder nur noch wenig Geld bringen, gleichzeitig aber Kosten für Server oder Updates aufwerfen, werden einfach abgestellt.
Codes in Plastikhüllen
Im Blogpost erwähnt Playstation noch die Möglichkeit, dass Spiele auch 2028 noch im Einzelhandel angeboten werden können: „in digitalen Formaten“. Wahrscheinlich sind damit Codes in Spieleverpackungen gemeint, so wie es bei Grand Theft Auto 6 bereits der Fall ist. Doch es ist davon auszugehen, dass das nur eine Übergangslösung ist. Die wenigsten Gamer dürften Interesse daran haben, sich Verpackungen zu kaufen, die nur einen Code enthalten.
Denn anders als etwa bei den Game Key Cards von Nintendo, für die es auch einige Kritik gab, können diese Codes nur einmalig verwendet werden. Einmal eingelöst, ist das Spiel dann an den jeweiligen Account gebunden. Ein Wiederverkauf ist nicht möglich. Und damit ist das wichtigste Argument für den Kauf physischer Medien hinfällig.
Mit diesem Schritt von Playstation dürfte zudem die Wahrscheinlichkeit steigen, dass eine Playstation 6 kein Disc-Laufwerk mehr verbaut haben wird. Sollte es so kommen, könnten somit auch keine älteren Playstation-Spiele, die noch auf Disc gekauft wurden, auf der neuen Konsole abgespielt werden. Auch sie werden somit wertlos.
Nach wie vor sind gebrauchte Spiele für viele Gamer die einzige Möglichkeit, sich überhaupt ein Spiel leisten zu können. Auch mit dem Wissen, dass sie ihr Spiel schließlich selbst wieder werden verkaufen können. Digitale Spiele, ob nun über den Playstation Store oder als Code in einer Plastikverpackung, verschließen auch diesen Zugang zum Gaming. Die Zukunft für Gamer dürfte also nicht nur in Bezug auf Hardware teuer werden.

articles.title: Nokia 100: características del celular de hace 15 años que siguen siendo útiles en 2026
articles.text:
El Nokia 100 llegó al mercado en 2011 continuando el legado de otros dispositivos de la marca, enfocados en funciones sencillas, dispositivos resistentes, con amplia batería e ideales para usuarios que no querían nada complejo.
Hoy en 2026, quince años después, este celular luce obsoleto al lado de dispositivos con IA, cámaras avanzadas, pantallas de casi 7 pulgadas y funciones plegables. Sin embargo, todo este progreso no hace inútil a un dispositivo que puede seguir funcionando para personas que quieren herramientas sencillas y alejarse de la conexión continua.
PUBLICIDAD
Cuáles son las características del Nokia 100
El Nokia 100 fue presentado como un teléfono GSM de banda dual, pensado para funcionar en redes 900/1800 o 850/1900, según la región. Su diseño compacto de 110 x 45.5 x 14.9 milímetros y peso de solo 69.6 gramos lo convertía en un aparato fácil de transportar y resistente al uso diario.
La pantalla TFT de 1.8 pulgadas, con resolución de 128 x 160 píxeles y 65.000 colores, ofrecía lo esencial para la lectura de mensajes y la navegación por menús simples.
PUBLICIDAD
A diferencia de los modelos más avanzados, el Nokia 100 carecía de conexión a internet, cámara fotográfica y funciones multimedia sofisticadas. Su sistema operativo Series 30 priorizaba la facilidad de uso, la autonomía y la durabilidad.
Entre sus colores disponibles se encontraban opciones como azul legionario, rosa festival, azul marino, negro fantasma y rojo coral, apelando a la personalización dentro de la sencillez.
PUBLICIDAD
El Nokia 100 concentraba sus prestaciones en funciones básicas pero útiles. Permitía realizar llamadas de voz y enviar mensajes SMS. Su agenda podía almacenar hasta 500 contactos y admitía la gestión de hasta cinco libretas de direcciones diferentes, facilitando el uso compartido del dispositivo entre varios miembros de una familia o grupo.
Una de las características más valoradas era la radio FM analógica, operativa con auriculares de 3,5 mm que funcionaban como antena. Esto permitía escuchar emisoras locales sin necesidad de conexión a internet, una ventaja crucial en regiones con infraestructura limitada o en situaciones de emergencia.
PUBLICIDAD
El teléfono incluía linterna LED integrada, activable rápidamente desde el teclado. Esta función se mantenía independiente del resto del sistema, lo que la hacía especialmente útil en cortes de luz o situaciones donde se requería iluminación inmediata y de bajo consumo energético.
En cuanto a herramientas organizativas, el Nokia 100 ofrecía alarma (que sonaba incluso con el equipo apagado), calendario, calculadora, cronómetro, temporizador y conversor de unidades. Juegos clásicos como el Snake Xenzia.
PUBLICIDAD
Uno de los puntos más destacados del Nokia 100 es su batería de larga duración. Equipado con una pila de iones de litio modelo BL-5CB de 800 mAh, podía alcanzar hasta 840 horas (35 días) en modo de espera y 7,2 horas de conversación continua.
Cómo podría ser útil el Nokia 100 en 2026
Con el apagón global de las redes 2G en gran parte de Estados Unidos, Europa y Asia, el Nokia 100 ha perdido su función principal de comunicación en muchas regiones. Donde las redes GSM han sido desmanteladas, el dispositivo ya no puede hacer ni recibir llamadas ni SMS.
PUBLICIDAD
En América Latina y algunos países de África y Asia, ciertas operadoras aún mantienen el 2G, aunque su desactivación es inminente.
A pesar de estas limitaciones, el Nokia 100 se mantiene vigente gracias a sus funciones offline. Su linterna, radio FM, alarma, reloj parlante y herramientas de organización siguen funcionando plenamente porque no dependen de la conectividad móvil ni de internet.
PUBLICIDAD
Además, la batería de larga duración y la resistencia física del dispositivo lo convierten en un aliado valioso para situaciones de emergencia, supervivencia o desconexión digital.
En 2026, el Nokia 100 ha encontrado nuevos propósitos. Puede usarse como parte de kits de emergencia, guardado en el automóvil o en mochilas de primeros auxilios, confiando en su linterna y radio FM para informar y asistir en crisis o catástrofes naturales.
PUBLICIDAD
El teléfono también destaca como despertador indestructible, perfecto para quienes desean evitar la tentación de revisar notificaciones durante la noche. Gracias a su alarma fiable, incluso con el dispositivo apagado, y su resistencia a caídas y golpes, supera ampliamente a los relojes inteligentes y a los smartphones en este aspecto.
PUBLICIDAD

articles.title: NVIDIA Reportedly Raises GDDR6 and GDDR7 Memory Kit Prices for RTX GPUs
articles.text:
Thursday, July 23rd 2026
	
		
	
	
	NVIDIA Reportedly Raises GDDR6 and GDDR7 Memory Kit Prices for RTX GPUs
NVIDIA has reportedly notified its add-in card partners of another GPU kit price increase, this time covering both GDDR7 and GDDR6 memory. This means the raise isn't limited to current Blackwell cards and could affect older GeForce products still using GDDR6 as well. The report comes from BenchLife via VideoCardz and follows a similar price adjustment for the RTX 5090 and RTX 5090D V2 back in May. NVIDIA supplies board partners with GPU and VRAM bundled together as a kit, so when memory costs go up, AIBs have little choice but to pass that along to retail pricing. BenchLife notes that partners are also seeing higher costs for coolers, PCBs, and packaging on top of the memory increases, though those secondary cost pressures are described as smaller than the memory-related ones.
The RTX 50 SUPER series is also affected by this. We've previously reported that those cards are on hold partly due to the cost of 3 GB GDDR7 modules. Inside sources say that each of those GDDR7 modules costs about $60-$70, roughly three times the cost of a 2 GB module at around $20. This adds a significant price premium on SUPER cards since the RTX 5070 SUPER was expected to be upgraded to offer 18 GB, while the RTX 5070 Ti SUPER and RTX 5080 SUPER would each provide 24 GB of GDDR7 memory. GPU prices have already increased 20-30% above where they were not long ago, and this latest round of kit price increases suggests there's more pressure to come. Previous-gen cards that use GDDR6 have been less affected up to now, but that appears to be changing.

articles.title: Geekbench 7 introduces biggest overhaul yet — real-world CPU testing, new media workloads, AI benchmarks, and CUDA support
articles.text:
Geekbench 7 introduces biggest overhaul yet — real-world CPU testing, new media workloads, AI benchmarks, and CUDA support
Multi-core testing gets a reality check.
Primate Labs has released Geekbench 7, the latest version of its popular cross-platform benchmark. The update introduces new and improved workloads designed to better represent and measure the performance of the latest CPUs and GPUs across major platforms, including Android, iOS, Windows, macOS, and Linux. Like previous versions, Geekbench 7 is available free of charge for personal use. Enthusiasts and IT professionals can also opt for Geekbench 7 Pro, which is available at a 20% discount until August 6.
One of the biggest changes introduced with Geekbench 7 is how the multi-core benchmark behaves. It will now mirror real-world application behavior instead of forcing every workload to use all available CPU cores. For instance, the HTML5 browser test has been excluded from the multi-core suite since web browsers are generally single- or lightly threaded. Geekbench 7 will only run a benchmark in multi-threaded mode if the real application it's modeling also uses multiple threads. As a result, Primate Labs says the new benchmark will deliver a more realistic indication of overall system performance.
Geekbench 7 will also feature a new set of media workloads designed to better evaluate how modern CPUs handle everyday multimedia tasks. These include encoding AV1 video for screen sharing during video calls, compressing audio using the Opus codec for applications such as voice recorders and podcasts, and decoding audio and video while simultaneously generating live captions using OpenAI's Whisper speech recognition model. Essentially, these workloads are claimed to better represent tasks such as video conferencing, content streaming, and media consumption.
A new Game Physics benchmark is also being added, which is based on the Jolt Physics engine used in modern games, to offer a more accurate measurement of CPU performance in physics-heavy gaming scenarios. The update further enhances its Photo Editor workload with more complex editing operations and expands the Photo Library test to include support for newer image formats such as JPEG XL and DNG.
The GPU benchmark has also been revamped to go beyond gaming, with greater emphasis on machine learning and content creation workloads. The new tests will measure tasks such as real-time face tracking and filter effects for social media apps, image upscaling using AI, and background blurring during video conferencing. Additionally, the update adds new GPU workloads for RAW image processing, LUT-based video color grading, path tracing, and fluid simulation.
Geekbench 7 is also set to introduce support for Nvidia's CUDA API in addition to OpenCL, Vulkan, and Metal, allowing users to benchmark Nvidia GPUs using the same API that is used in a variety of professional and AI applications.
Lastly, in order to keep up with demanding modern workloads, the benchmark datasets have been updated to better reflect the larger and more complex files that users work with today. For instance, the File Compression test now includes a broader mix of archives containing source code, object code, and text documents, while the PDF Viewer workload processes a wider range of files, from park maps to technical documentation and academic papers. The update also introduces more assets and additional image formats across its developer and image processing workloads.

articles.title: How long will Star Wars Zero Company be? Will it have New Game Plus? Can I have a whole team of Clone Troopers? Bit Reactor has answered all your questions
articles.text:
Star Wars Zero Company takes 30-40 hours to beat 'depending on your difficulty level and experience with the strategy genre' but won't have a New Game Plus mode
There are no plans for microtransactions
- Star Wars Zero Company will take 30-40 hours to beat the main campaign
- The game won't feature New Game Plus mode, romance systems, or branching story paths
- Post-launch content is also unconfirmed at this time
Bit Reactor has confirmed that Star Wars Zero Company will take up to 40 hours to finish, and it won't have a New Game Plus mode.
The single-player turn-based tactics game is one of my most anticipated titles of the year, and ahead of its launch next month, the studio has conducted a community Q&A to answer a long series of questions.
One of the first questions asked how long the campaign will be, and lead producer Caydence Funk has confirmed that "Depending on your difficulty level and experience with the strategy genre," it's estimated that it can take between 30 and 40 hours for the average player to beat.
It's also confirmed that the story will be linear with no romance systems or branching paths.
"While we are excited about pushing the genre forward with a more cinematic approach, this is still a turn-based tactics game at its heart where adept skill and strategy are needed to overcome tense combat challenges," Bit Reactor said. "That said, there are story moments that can alter based on who you have in your squad, but the overall story is a linear one from beginning to end."
Personally, 40 hours is the ideal length, and a linear story means I can experience everything the story without having to worry about missing out on additional storylines.
"As far as exploration goes, yes, you’ll have the ability to explore a section of some planets prior to engaging in turn-based combat on them," the studio added.
Sign up for breaking news, reviews, opinion, top tech deals, and more.
"This is a minor facet of the game that we feel adds a unique, immersive quality to Star Wars Zero Company. These small segments are a chance for you, as Hawks, to conduct the espionage that Zero Company excels at, and are main-story-only segments that can affect the subsequent combat by granting Intel and Advantage Points."
Unfortunately, the game won't launch with New Game Plus mode, so new playthroughs will have to be completely fresh, "but players will unlock certain customization options on subsequent playthroughs" through progress.
Zero Company is set during one of my favorite Star Wars eras, the Clone Wars, so I'm very excited to experience a new story during this time period.
We can expect battles across the galaxy with the Separatist Alliance, a team consisting of a Clone Trooper, a Mandalorian, a Jedi Padawan, an Umbaran sniper, and more, as well as the appearance of Anakin Skywalker.
Customization will also play a big role in the game, and while players can't have an entire team of Clone Troopers, Bit Reactor confirmed that you'll have access to Clone armor cosmetics with the ability to customize your team's armor from the start. Outfits don't impact gameplay, but Clone Trooper helmets will provide a voice modulation effect, which sounds neat!
Even cooler, The Clone Wars TV series voice actor Dee Bradley Baker will provide his iconic voice to the character Trick and additional Clone Troopers, but the full cast has yet to be announced.
As for additional content, good news, there are no plans for microtransactions to be added to the game; however, the "Arc Trooper" Armor Set is only part of the "Grand Army of the Republic" Cosmetic Pack for the Deluxe Edition, but players will still have access to other cosmetic options in the base game.
The game also won't have mod support, and "right now" post-launch content isn't confirmed because Bit Reactor is "focused on making the best game we can at launch."
Star Wars Zero Company launches on August 27 for PC, PlayStation 5, Xbox Series X, and Series S.

articles.title: Paso a paso para invertir en criptomonedas y cuál es su valor este jueves 23 de julio
articles.text:
Las criptomonedas son un activo digital innovador que han experimentado un crecimiento monumental en los últimos tiempos debido a varios elementos que contribuyen a ello, entre ellos que algunos gobiernos hayan decidido darles una oportunidad como moneda de curso legal; no obstante, también han sufrido descalabros que han puesto en duda su viabilidad, como el más reciente episodio conocido como el "criptoinvierno".
Pese a este panorama, cada vez más personas han empezado a adquirir criptomonedas para poder invertir en algo "seguro" y "fiable" tanto a corto como a largo plazo, a pesar de los niveles extremos de inestabilidad que sufre constantemente.
PUBLICIDAD
Sin embargo, invertir o comprar en criptodivisas es más fácil de lo que parece. Hay que recordar que se trata de monedas virtuales, por lo que serán controladas en carteras o monederos que comparten esa particularidad, pues a diferencia del dinero corriente, no tienen un soporte físico.
El precio de las criptomonedas hoy
Esta es la cotización de las criptodivisas más destacadas en este momento.
El Bitcoin, cotiza a 65.404,72 dólares, lo que implicó un cambio de -1,053% en las últimas horas.
La segunda criptomoneda más popular del mercado, Ethereum, ha mostrado un movimiento de -0,958% en las últimas 24 horas, por lo que su valor se ubica en 1.914,97 dólares.
PUBLICIDAD
En el caso de TetherUs, su precio es de 1 dólares, por lo que en el último día tuvo un movimiento de -0%.
Por su parte, BNB, tiene un valor de 568,68 dólares, con un cambio de -0,86%, en cambio el Litecoin cotizó a 46.93 dólares, tras una variación de 0.24371508.
PUBLICIDAD
Finalmente, el Dogecoin, una de las monedas virtuales que fue impulsada por Elon Musk, tiene un valor de 0,07 dólares tras presentar un cambio de -1,38% en las últimas 24 horas.
Qué pasa con las criptodivisas
Luego de que en las primeras semanas de mayo del 2022 se viviera el "criptocrash" o "criptoinvierno" que dejaron al descubierto la enorme volatilidad de estas monedas digitales, ha llegado un nuevo periodo de relativa estabilidad.
PUBLICIDAD
Bitcoin, ethereum y BNB han mostrado variaciones "controladas", puesto que no se han disparado los precios como en semanas previas. Por ejemplo, a inicios de agosto, las mencionadas anteriormente tuvieron un cambio menor del 2%.
Por otra parte, algo que esta llamando la atención en el mundo de las criptomonedas es que China está ablandando sus restricciones y podría comenzar a permitir su uso. Específicamente sería Hong Kong en donde este cambio se haría presente.
PUBLICIDAD
Sumado a ello, la plataforma de transacciones digitales PayPal anunció su propia stablecoin llamada PayPal USD (PYUSD), que cuenta por el respaldo de depósitos en dólares, bonos del Tesoro de Estados Unidos a corto plazo y activos equivalentes.
La compañía ha afirmado en su declaración que permitirá la transferencia de fondos a monederos digitales de terceros y proporcionará detalles sobre cómo integrar su servicio en exchanges centralizados y descentralizados, con el objetivo de ser utilizado en Finanzas Descentralizadas (DeFi, por sus siglas en inglés). Por lo tanto, es muy probable que se utilice ampliamente en la industria Web3.
PUBLICIDAD
Su avance en Latinoamérica
Criptomonedas en México: el Banco de México (Banxico) ha determinado que ninguna de las instituciones que participan en el sistema financiero nacional podrá hacer uso o deberá permitir operaciones de ninguna clase a través de este medio de pago.
En territorio mexicano el empresario Ricardo Salinas Pliego, uno de los más ricos del país, ha mostrado interés en las criptomonedas y ha asegurado que varios de sus negocios aceptarán bitcoin en el futuro, incluido su banco; hasta el momento una de sus tiendas más populares ya lo hace.
PUBLICIDAD
Criptomonedas en Perú: el Banco Central de Reserva del Perú (BCR) ha dejado en claro que su misión no es ser el primero ni el segundo banco central que regule el uso de las criptomonedas, ello debido a la inestabilidad que las caracteriza. Sin embargo, hace días el presidente del (BCR) aseguró que el BCR trabajaba en un proyecto de moneda digital propia.
Criptomonedas en Colombia: en la nación sudamericana hay más de 500 sitios donde es permitido pagar con criptodivisas. Colombia ocupa el puesto 14 entre 26 países de adopción de criptomonedas, según el informe de Finder.
PUBLICIDAD
Criptomonedas en Centroamérica: en el gobierno de El Salvador, el bitcoin, que en septiembre de 2021 se convirtió en moneda de curso legal, ha perdido oficialmente este estatus en este enero del 2025 tras una reforma aprobada por la Asamblea Legislativa del país. Según informó la prensa local, la modificación de la Ley Bitcoin fue impulsada por el gobierno del presidente Nayib Bukele y respaldada por la mayoría oficialista en el órgano legislativo. Este cambio marca el fin de una política que había colocado al país centroamericano en el centro del debate global sobre las criptomonedas.
¿Cómo crear una criptomoneda?
Al momento de crear una criptomoneda es importante primero determinar qué se desea tener: una moneda o un token. La primera usa su propia blockchain, mientras que la segunda se basa en una red preexistente.
De acuerdo con el sitio de Binance, para crear una criptomoneda se necesita de un gran equipo de desarrolladores y expertos; mientras que para el token sí se requieren conocimientos técnicos pero es posible crearlo en minutos a través del uso de otras blockchains como Ethereum o BNB, que son las más populares.
Los costos de creación, el tiempo requerido y el uso de fuerza de trabajo dependerá de si se opta por hacer una moneda virtual o un token. En éste último caso también se puede usar un código establecido para crear tokens o pagar para usar un servicio de creación de monedas.
Es importante saber que antes de crear una criptomoneda se debe considerar su utilidad y estado legal.
En el caso de elegir crear una criptomoneda, entonces se debe elegir una blockchain, posteriormente se debe hacer un plan acorde al funcionamiento y la funcionalidad de la blockchain para diseñar los nodos y la interfaz.

articles.title: Valve's Steam Deck price hike has completely destroyed sales, new data suggests
articles.text:
Death of Gaming: Just like any other company dealing in hardware products built from off-the-shelf components, Valve is facing some truly difficult choices when it comes to pricing. The company tried to fend off the chip shortage caused by the AI boom with a massive price increase, but potential customers apparently responded by removing themselves from the buying equation.
A recent report by Boiling Steam might confirm what most enthusiasts have always suspected: an overpriced Steam Deck is never going to sell well. In fact, Valve's handheld machine might have already suffered a disastrous drop in sales. Despite the price hike, Valve is earning far less money than it did before.
Boiling Steam used the same methodology it employed to estimate Steam Machine sales, tracking data points from Steam's own global list of best-selling games and products. The outlet compared the Steam Deck's ranking throughout 2025, when it was often listed fairly high on the sales chart. Things changed in 2026, when Valve decided to retire the older – and cheaper – LCD models and offer only the OLED models at a significantly higher price.
At first, OLED Steam Decks appeared to sell out despite the $300 price hike. According to new estimates from Boiling Steam, sales have now undergone yet another dramatic change. Valve is selling 82% fewer units than it did in 2025. Steam Deck sales have allegedly fallen from 11,000 – 18,000 units per week to an average of 1,400 – 3,000 units per week.
Valve tried to offset the massive increase in component prices by passing the supply-chain surcharge on to customers. According to Boiling Steam's estimates, the company is now suffering from a 72% drop in revenue as well. Despite the price hike, Valve might have significantly diminished the Steam Deck's appeal as an enticing option for handheld gaming enthusiasts.
Boiling Steam speculates that the Steam Deck was an interesting option when it sold for $650 but is a complete waste of money when priced at around $1,000 for the 1TB model. Furthermore, affluent gamers looking for a handheld at that price point will likely gravitate toward more powerful machines, such as the MSI Claw 8 EX AI+ or the Asus ROG Ally X.
If the publication's methodology checks out, we might soon see a dramatic collapse in Steam Machine sales as well. The IT industry is currently going through a series of massive transformations, which means it's probably too early to say that the Steam Deck is completely finished. After all, Valve engineers recently confirmed that things can always get worse.

articles.title: From Period Taboos to Mushroom Farms: How Dr Surbhi Empowers Bihar’s Women
articles.text:
From Period Taboos to Mushroom Farms: How Dr Surbhi Empowers Bihar’s Women
Dr Surbhi Kumari’s SumArth has educated thousands about menstrual health while helping rural women build sustainable incomes through mushroom farming.
In the villages of Bihar, a new beginning of awareness regarding menstruation has now started to become visible. Many women and adolescent girls are speaking openly about periods, obtaining correct information, and leaving behind the old hesitation associated with it. Behind this change are the continuous efforts of certain people who went village to village to begin a dialogue and gave the message of connecting menstruation with health and dignity. Taking this very initiative forward, a campaign is also being run to make women economically self-reliant by connecting them with mushroom farming. This is not merely a social initiative, but an effort to strengthen a new way of thinking about awareness, dignity and self-reliance.
Among the people through whose sustained efforts this change is becoming possible, one prominent name is also that of Dr. Surbhi Kumari.
Dr. Surbhi Kumari, who is the co-founder of SumArth (MicroX Foundation), was once associated with journalism. Today she is writing a new story of change in the villages of Bihar, connecting together women's health, dignity and livelihood. From open conversation on periods to making women economically self-reliant through mushroom farming, her initiative is becoming a new example of awareness and empowerment in society.
This initiative of hers has come forward at a time when the situation regarding menstrual hygiene in India has improved, but challenges still remain. According to the National Family Health Survey (NFHS-5, 2019-21), about 78 percent of young women aged 15-24 in the country use safe menstrual hygiene products. However, in rural areas both awareness and availability are still major challenges.
The Journey From Journalism to Social Service
Dr. Surbhi Kumari was born into an ordinary joint family in Gaya district of Bihar. The family was large and the financial resources limited. Her grandfather had retired from government service, and the expenses of the entire family were run on that same income. Despite the difficult circumstances, the family considered education to be the biggest investment. This very thinking became the foundation of her personality.
After completing her school education from Nazareth Academy in Gaya, she did her graduation in Communicative English and Media Studies from Patna Women's College. After this she completed her post-graduation in Journalism and Mass Communication, and then completed her PhD while researching on the subject of women's health and menstrual awareness.
During her time in journalism she reported on many social issues. She listened to people's problems and placed their stories before the country. But with time she realised that only writing about problems is not enough; it is also necessary to become a part of the solution.
In conversation with YourStory, Dr. Surbhi says, "Journalism gave me the opportunity to see people's lives closely. But a time came when I felt that change would not come merely from writing about problems. I wanted to live and work among those people whose stories I was writing. That is when I decided that now, along with the pen, I must also work on the ground."
During the Covid-19 pandemic she returned to her home in Gaya. It was here, during conversations with rural women, that she came to know that during menstruation many women would not work in the fields for four to five days. The reason was not only the shortage of sanitary pads; the lack of information and social hesitation were equally big problems.
This very experience became the decisive turning point of her life.
The Beginning of Breaking the Silence on Periods in Villages
Dr. Surbhi started menstrual awareness sessions in the villages. But the beginning was not easy at all.
Many times mothers would take their daughters home from the middle of the programme. Some men would call their wives back, saying that such subjects should not be discussed publicly.
It was then that she understood that the biggest problem was not the lack of information, but the silence that had been going on for years.
It was from here that programmes like Periodshala, SABLA and Pad Yatra began. The objective of these initiatives was not only to give information to girls, but to make the family, teachers, men and the entire community a part of this dialogue.
The padyatras (foot marches) taken out in the villages bring people together. After this, myths related to menstruation are discussed through street plays, community meetings and open dialogue.
UNICEF too believes that menstruation is not merely a subject of health. It is also connected with education, dignity, equal opportunity and women's participation. According to experts, only when men and families become a part of this conversation does lasting change come about in social behaviour.
Dr. Surbhi says, "In the beginning people used to say that talking about periods is wrong. But we did not give up. We understood that change would not come from girls alone. Only when family, men, teachers and the whole society come together will the silence break. Today those same villages are talking openly. This is our biggest success."
In many villages she met women who had seen a sanitary pad for the first time in their lives. Her team then did not limit itself to awareness alone, and also began working on the availability of sanitary pads at the local level and on the livelihood model connected with it.
When Awareness Became the Greatest Force of Change
Dr. Surbhi believes that the success of any social initiative should be measured not only by figures, but by the change that comes about in people's behaviour.
In the past few years her team has delivered menstrual health related information to more than 30,000 women and more than 10,000 adolescent girls across various districts of Bihar.
But for her, the biggest achievement is not the figures, but the change that has come about in thinking.
During one padyatra, many boys of the village were hesitating even to take a sanitary pad in their hands. They thought that it was only a women's thing. Some time later, those very boys became part of the awareness campaign across the entire village with sanitary pads in their hands, and began explaining to people that menstruation is a normal biological process.
Dr. Surbhi says, "We often think that menstruation is only a women's subject. But that is not so. When boys, fathers, teachers and families become a part of this conversation, only then does real change come. I have seen with my own eyes that the children who earlier hesitated even to touch a sanitary pad later began spreading awareness throughout the village."
One incident still makes her emotional.
A woman told her that she deliberately did not bathe during menstruation. She thought that the foul smell coming from her body would keep her husband away from her.
After several counselling sessions, she not only adopted correct menstrual hygiene, but also began speaking openly about her health, her rights and her self-respect.
Mushroom Farming Gave Women a New Identity
SumArth's identity is not limited only to period awareness.
The organisation's very beginning was made with the objective of strengthening women's economic self-reliance. For this, the team chose mushroom farming.
According to the Indian Council of Agricultural Research (ICAR), mushroom production can be started in less space, at low cost and in less time. This is the reason it is seen as an effective income-raising model for women's self-help groups and small farmers.
Dr. Surbhi and her team prepared low-cost, climate-friendly mushroom huts made locally from bamboo and kusha grass. These naturally maintain temperature and moisture, due to which dependence on electricity is reduced and production becomes possible throughout the year.
The organisation does not give training alone, but also connects women with technical support, markets and entrepreneurship.
One of the most inspiring stories connected with this initiative is that of Lalsa Devi.
Lalsa Devi, who comes from the Mahadalit community, did not even have a pucca (permanent) house to live in. With SumArth's help she built a climate-friendly mushroom hut, took training, and started mushroom production.
Today she is earning a regular income and has become an inspiration for the other women of her village.
Dr. Surbhi says, "When a woman's first earning comes into her own hands, it is not only her economic condition that changes, her self-confidence changes too. Her voice begins to be heard within the family. For us, mushroom farming is not merely employment, but a medium for giving women dignity and identity."
A Shared Dream of Health, Dignity and Livelihood
Dr. Surbhi believes that the biggest challenge even today is the lack of resources.
Many schools, panchayats and government institutions want to invite her organisation, but because of limited funding it is not possible to reach every place.
She believes that social change does not come from any single workshop. For this, continuous dialogue with the community has to be maintained over a long period of time.
In the coming years, her plan is to take Periodshala, SABLA and Pad Yatra beyond Bihar to other states. Along with this, connecting thousands of women with climate-friendly mushroom farming is her goal.
She wants to develop such a model that in future other organisations and government institutions may also adopt it. With this very objective, her team is also paying special attention to research and documentation.
Dr. Surbhi says, "My dream is that such a society be built where no girl leaves school because of periods, no woman compromises on her health due to a lack of information, and every rural woman has the opportunity of a dignified livelihood. When health, education and economic self-reliance walk together, only then does lasting change come about in society."
The World Bank too believes that when women's economic participation increases, it is not only the income of families that rises, but there is also a positive impact on the local economy, on education and on social development.
Today, when there is fresh discussion on women's health and economic empowerment in rural India, the journey of Dr. Surbhi Kumari conveys an important message.
Change does not always come from grand plans. Sometimes it begins with a question. Sometimes with an open conversation. Sometimes with a padyatra taken out through the lanes of a village. And sometimes with a small mushroom hut.
These very small steps together bring big change into the lives of thousands of women. This is SumArth's greatest story.

articles.title: Senior White House official accuses Moonshot AI of copying Anthropic's leading frontier model - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
Senior White House official accuses Moonshot AI of copying Anthropic’s leading frontier model
A senior White House official has accused Chinese artificial intelligence startup Moonshot AI of using so-called “distillation” techniques to essentially pirate the capabilities of Anthropic PBC’s most powerful models in its own, open-source AI systems.
“We have information that Moonshot AI distilled Anthropic’s Fable for the development of its K3 model,” Michael Kratsios (pictured), director of the White House Office of Science and Technology Policy, said in a post on X on Wednesday.
Kratsios was referring to Moonshot AI’s new Kimi K3 model, which was pronounced the world’s largest open-weights model when it was released last week to great fanfare thanks to its prowess, which matches some of the capabilities of Anthropic’s and OpenAI Group PBC’s best AI systems. He added that the company went to great lengths to hide what it had done.
“To do this they developed a sophisticated internal platform to conduct large-scale distillation against U.S. models, allowing them to quickly switch between multiple methods of access to avoid detection,” he claimed.
Experts say Kimi K3 is the most advanced open-weights model released so far, performing at the same level, or sometimes even above that of other leading frontier models in multiple benchmarks. But whereas Anthropic and OpenAI intend to charge for access to their best models, having spent billions of dollars to develop them, Moonshot AI plans to make Kimi K3 freely available for anyone to download, run and customize on their own servers or devices.
What did Moonshot AI allegedly do?
Kratsios claims that Moonshot AI used a machine learning compression method known as distillation to transfer knowledge from Fable 5 to Kimi K3. In distillation, a larger “teacher” model is used to train a smaller “student” model. Rather than learn only from basic right-or-wrong answers, the student model learns from the teacher model’s full probability distributions – for instance, a 90% chance for word A, 8% for word B – which reveal clues about how the teacher thinks.
Distillation is sometimes used in “legitimate” ways, Kratsios said. For instance, some AI labs use the technique to train less powerful models on the outputs of a more powerful one to make more efficient versions of the same AI systems. “Legitimate AI distillation used to create smaller, more efficient models plays a vital role in this open innovation ecosystem,” he said. “However, large-scale, covert industrial distillation aimed at stealing proprietary U.S. technology and undermining American research is unacceptable.”
Kratsios’ comments come just days after U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said that the U.S. government could sanction Chinese AI model makers if proof emerges that they basically copied American-made models to develop their own. They’re notable, because they represent a rare instance in which the Trump administration has appeared to be supportive of Anthropic.
There has been a lot of antagonism between the White House and the AI firm recently, with officials recently preventing the company from releasing Fable 5 due to security concerns. Prior to that, in February, the Pentagon blacklisted Anthropic after it was refused full access to its leading frontier models.
“Thanks @mkratsios47 for speaking out on this important issue,” Sarah Heck, Anthropic’s head of public policy, wrote in a reply to Kratsios’s post on X.
Heck added that Anthropic is continuing to work with the government to try to prevent U.S. models from being distilled by Chinese firms. “Illicit, adversarial distillation is IP theft and industrial espionage that supports adversary military and intelligence capabilities,” she wrote. “It is a national challenge that creates serious national security risks for the United States and democratic allies.”
Anthropic first accused Chinese firms of abusing the distillation process in February, pointing fingers at Moonshot AI, MiniMax and DeepSeek Ltd. and calling on the U.S. government to take action to prevent it. But while White House officials paid lip service, Anthropic did not get much sympathy from the general public, which noted the irony of the allegations, given that it trained its systems on massive volumes of copyrighted data posted online.
Experts are skeptical
Despite getting Kratsios’ support, there are many who believe that distillation cannot be responsible for the advanced capabilities of Kimi K3. For instance, Braden Hancock, a researcher at the Laude Institute and the co-founder of AI startup Snorkel AI Inc., told TechCrunch that it would be almost impossible to train a model as strong as Kimi K3 on Fable 5 so quickly. “There’s just not even frankly time, right?” he said. “Fable’s only been publicly available since July 1st. You can’t distill that much data, train a model, and release it in two weeks.”
Another expert, Nathan Lambert, who is a researcher at the Allen Institute for AI, was similarly skeptical that Moonshot AI could have pulled it off so quickly. “I’ve been of the opinion that distillation has becoming less and less impactful over time as the Chinese models get closer to the frontier and the training regime shifts to [reinforcement learning],” he said in a podcast this week. “[If] it were the case, everyone would be easily able to catch up to a GLM or to a K3 by using its data for distillation. But we have not, or we won’t see this, from supervised fine-tuning alone.”
Given that the White House claims to have “evidence” of Moonshot AI’s guilt, the next question is whether the government will actually follow through on Bessent’s threat to start sanctioning Chinese AI companies. Moonshot AI has not commented on the allegations, but a spokesperson at the Chinese embassy in Washington D.C. told Reuters that the claims are “entirely unfounded.”
“Relevant individuals in the United States should respect the facts, discard prejudice and stop smearing and discrediting China’s achievements in the development of its artificial intelligence industry,” the spokesperson said.

articles.title: This devious malware scans over 300 apps to build an AI profile telling hackers which victims to target
articles.text:
This devious malware scans over 300 apps to build an AI profile telling hackers which victims to target
Malware now talks directly to its boss
- Varonis Threat Labs uncovered Dolphin X, a powerful RAT with 329 features across 10 categories
- Its standout “AI Profiler” ranks victims by usage and sends summaries to attackers daily
- Malware is sold on the dark web via subscription tiers, starting at $80 per month
What if malware could talk to its operator and tell it which of the infected victims is worth paying attention to, and which not? A few years ago, this might have been science fiction but today, thanks to breakthroughs in Artificial Intelligence (AI), not only is it possible, it’s also already available on the black market.
Security researchers Varonis Threat Labs recently disclosed finding a rather revolutionary remote access trojan (RAT) called Dolphin X.
Even without advanced AI capabilities, the RAT is quite potent, acting as an infostealer, a Hidden Virtual Network Computing (HVNC), a DDoS botnet, or a loader. Just its infostealer capabilities are nothing short of impressive - it can target more than 300 applications to steal browser passwords, enterprise credentials, cryptocurrency wallet data, DevOps secrets, and different sensitive files, and it comes with 329 features split into 10 categories.
AI Profiler
However, the AI capability is the one that stunned the researchers. Called “AI Profiler”, the feature ranks victims by app usage, browsing history, and more, sending a daily summary to the attackers.
The malware is now being offered on the dark web, where other criminals can subscribe to one of three tiers. The basic tier costs $80 per month, while the top tier is around $230 per month. Lifetime subscription costs $1,140 for basic access, and goes up to $3,420 for the top tier.
"Dolphin X’s collection scope reaches well beyond browser passwords to SSH keys, cloud tokens, and DevOps credentials," Varonis said in its write-up. "On the wrong machine, a single infection could expose access to an entire production environment."
"Its use of AI is also interesting because it shows us how AI is being integrated into more cybercrime tooling."

articles.title: AI memory shortage is now increasing the price of cars — GM warns of vast cost increases, BYD hikes driver assistance prices 20%
articles.text:
AI memory shortage is now increasing the price of cars — GM warns of vast cost increases, BYD hikes driver assistance prices 20%
The impact of the memory chip shortage is going beyond computers and consumer electronics.
While PC builders, enthusiasts, and gamers are some of the most heavily affected by the AI-driven memory chip shortage, experts have also been warning that this will eventually hit the automotive sector. It seems that their fears have come true, as Nikkei Asia reports that two major automakers are increasing their prices precisely for this reason. General Motors said that it expects new vehicle prices to increase by 0.3% this year, changing its previous projection of vehicle costs to remain the same or even slightly more affordable. On the other side of the world, Chinese automotive giant BYD has also raised the prices of the driver assistance features by 20%, which it sells separately from its models. South Korea’s Hyundai also called on domestic chip manufacturers to strengthen the local supply chain.
GM Chief Financial Officer Paul Jacobson said during the carmaker’s earnings call that GM expects its costs to increase by $1.5 to $2 billion, which is mostly driven by increasing prices of vehicle components, especially DRAM. While most people wouldn’t equate cars with memory chips, the increasing number of features and technologies that buyers expect from new models means that engineers and designers must add more memory compared to models from the past.
Micron said in 2023 that the average vehicle used 90GB of DRAM and NAND, and it’s expecting this combined requirement to jump to 278GB by 2026, with high-end models requiring up to 2TB. A British OEM broke down the memory requirements of vehicles released this year — infotainment systems require between 4GB and 16GB, ADAS and safety systems need 8GB to 32GB, while centralized systems often have a minimum requirement of 16GB and could go as high as 64GB or more. And as AI assistants start becoming available on cars, these systems will require at least 256GB of memory. In fact, Micron predicts that cars with level 4 autonomy will need at least 300GB of RAM, as they’re essentially supercomputers on wheels.
Note that automotive memory isn’t just any high-end chip that you can get from wafer production lines. Instead, these are specialized parts that take months or years to be validated for vehicle use. That’s because they must withstand various environmental factors that cars go through, from weather and constant road vibrations to extreme heat and cold.
All this means that the current memory chip shortage will have an outsize effect on the automotive industry and push prices even higher. This is bad news for the average car buyer, who is already facing record-high prices for new vehicles. And if the chip shortages continue, we might experience delays in vehicle deliveries and a lack of availability worse than what we experienced in 2021 during the height of port closures due to the pandemic.

Jowi Morales is a tech enthusiast with years of experience working in the industry. He’s been writing with several tech publications since 2021, where he’s been interested in tech hardware and consumer electronics.
